256	    @staticmethod
257	    def _diff_apt_packages(
258	        source_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
259	        target_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
260	        hold_pin_facts: Sequence[HoldPinFact],
261	        unavailable_item_ids: frozenset[str],
262	        source_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
263	        target_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
264	    ) -> list[ItemDiff]:
265	        """One diff per item id present on either side, source-then-target order,
266	        followed by the `apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D5/D8 — holds emitted AFTER
267	        package diffs so install lands before its hold once the diffs converge).
268	
269	        Precedence per package id: a PINNED package (present on the target and named by a
270	        pin fact) yields `HELD_OR_PINNED`/`REPORT_ONLY` — the pin echo D-25 requires,
271	        informational only. A HELD package (target hold set) has its install/upgrade
272	        action SUPPRESSED (a held package is never proposed for install/version change)
273	        but produces NO package-level report — the hold travels as its own `apt:hold:`
274	        item, so a held package is never double-reported. Otherwise: missing-on-target ->
275	        `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` if apt reports no candidate, else `MISSING_ON_TARGET`/`INSTALL`;
276	        extra-on-target -> `EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`REMOVE`; present on both with differing
277	        versions -> `VERSION_MISMATCH`/`REPORT_ONLY` (D-04: reported, never
278	        force-downgraded); present on both with equal versions -> no diff at all.
279	
280	        Hold membership (D2): source-held & target-not -> `AptHoldItem` INSTALL (hold);
281	        target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or neither -> no diff.
282	        """
283	        source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
284	        target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
285	
286	        # PINS only (#208, D5): holds no longer key this guard — they travel as their own
287	        # `apt:hold:` items below, so this branch keys purely on the pin mechanism.
288	        pinned: dict[str, HoldPinFact] = {}
289	        for fact in hold_pin_facts:
290	            if fact.mechanism == "pin":
291	                pinned.setdefault(fact.package, fact)
292	
293	        seen: dict[str, None] = {}
294	        for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
295	            seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
296	
297	        diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
298	        for item_id in seen:
299	            source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
300	            target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
301	
302	            if target_item is not None and target_item.name in pinned:
303	                diffs.append(
304	                    ItemDiff(
305	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
306	                        diff_class=DiffClass.HELD_OR_PINNED,
307	                        action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
308	                        item_id=item_id,
309	                        label=target_item.label(),
310	                        detail=build_held_or_pinned_detail(pinned[target_item.name]),
311	                    )
312	                )
313	            elif target_item is not None and target_item.name in target_hold_names:
314	                # Held on the target: suppress its install/version action entirely (a held
315	                # package must never be proposed for install/upgrade). No package-level
316	                # report — the `apt:hold:` item below carries the hold fact.
317	                continue
318	            elif source_item is not None and target_item is None:
319	                if item_id in unavailable_item_ids:
320	                    diffs.append(
321	                        ItemDiff(
322	                            item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
323	                            diff_class=DiffClass.REPO_UNAVAILABLE,
324	                            action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
325	                            item_id=item_id,
326	                            label=source_item.label(),
327	                            detail=build_repo_unavailable_detail(source_item.name),
328	                        )
329	                    )
330	                else:
331	                    diffs.append(
332	                        ItemDiff(
333	                            item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
334	                            diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET,
335	                            action=DiffAction.INSTALL,
336	                            item_id=item_id,
337	                            label=source_item.label(),
338	                            detail=None,
339	                        )
340	                    )
341	            elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
342	                diffs.append(
343	                    ItemDiff(
344	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
345	                        diff_class=DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
346	                        action=DiffAction.REMOVE,
347	                        item_id=item_id,
348	                        label=target_item.label(),
349	                        detail=None,
350	                    )
351	                )
352	            elif source_item is not None and target_item is not None and source_item.version != target_item.version:
353	                diffs.append(
354	                    ItemDiff(
355	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
356	                        diff_class=DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH,
357	                        action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
358	                        item_id=item_id,
359	                        label=target_item.label(),
360	                        detail=build_version_mismatch_detail(source_item.version, target_item.version),
361	                    )
362	                )
363	            # else: present on both, equal versions, not held/pinned -> no diff.
364	
365	        # Hold membership diffs (#208, D2/D8): emitted AFTER every package diff so a
366	        # package install lands before its hold when both are approved.
367	        diffs.extend(PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_holds(source_hold_names, target_hold_names))
368	        return diffs
369	
370	    @staticmethod
371	    def _diff_apt_holds(source_hold_names: frozenset[str], target_hold_names: frozenset[str]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
372	        """`apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D2): source-held & target-not -> INSTALL
373	        (hold); target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or on neither
374	        -> no diff. `sorted` for a stable, deterministic review order.
375	        """
376	        diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
377	        for name in sorted(source_hold_names | target_hold_names):
378	            in_source = name in source_hold_names
379	            in_target = name in target_hold_names
380	            if in_source == in_target:
381	                continue
382	            hold_item = AptHoldItem(name=name)
383	            diffs.append(
384	                ItemDiff(
385	                    item_class=ItemClass.APT_HOLD,
386	                    diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET if in_source else DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
387	                    action=DiffAction.INSTALL if in_source else DiffAction.REMOVE,
388	                    item_id=hold_item.item_id,
389	                    label=hold_item.label(),
390	                    detail=None,
391	                )
392	            )
393	        return diffs
394	
395	    def _build_review_groups(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> tuple[ReviewGroup, ...]:
396	        """One `ReviewGroup` per `(action, item_class)` present in `diffs`, keyed on
397	        `(manager, action)` for the reviewer's removal-direction test (D-24) so removals
398	        never share a group with installs. The title's verb and every entry's
399	        `action_label` come from `_ACTION_VOCABULARY`, keyed by the group's own item
400	        class — so a block-state membership item (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`,
401	        `flatpak:mask:`) whose add direction shares the `INSTALL` action with a package
402	        still reads "Hold/Mask ..." rather than displaying under "Install packages"
403	        (#208). Grouping by item class as well as action is what keeps that verb correct
404	        when one action mixes item classes (e.g. apt package INSTALL alongside apt hold
405	        INSTALL); the group's `action` value stays the raw `DiffAction` so add-direction
406	        stays default-checked and remove-direction lands in its own unticked group.
407	
408	        Emission order: `_ACTION_ORDER` (install, change, remove, report) outer, and
409	        within one action the item classes in first-seen order — which, because
410	        `_diff_apt_packages` emits package diffs before hold diffs, keeps a package group
411	        ahead of its hold group.
412	        """
413	        by_key: dict[tuple[DiffAction, ItemClass], list[ItemDiff]] = {}
414	        class_order: dict[DiffAction, list[ItemClass]] = {}
415	        for diff in diffs:
416	            key = (diff.action, diff.item_class)
417	            if key not in by_key:
418	                by_key[key] = []
419	                class_order.setdefault(diff.action, []).append(diff.item_class)
420	            by_key[key].append(diff)
421	
422	        groups: list[ReviewGroup] = []
423	        for action in _ACTION_ORDER:
424	            for item_class in class_order.get(action, []):
425	                entries = by_key[(action, item_class)]
426	                # REPORT_ONLY has no more-specific per-item-class meaning for any current
427	                # manager (IN-01): fall back to "report" rather than the raw enum value
428	                # ("report_only"), which read awkwardly in review text like "Report_only
429	                # flatpak packages". Every other action still falls back to its own
430	                # `action.value`, unchanged.
431	                default_verb = "report" if action == DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY else action.value
432	                verb = _ACTION_VOCABULARY.get((item_class, action), default_verb)
433	                groups.append(
434	                    ReviewGroup(
435	                        manager=self.manager_id,
436	                        action=action.value,
437	                        title=f"{verb.capitalize()} {self.manager_id} packages",
438	                        entries=tuple(
439	                            ReviewEntry(item_id=diff.item_id, label=diff.label, action_label=verb, detail=diff.detail)
440	                            for diff in entries
441	                        ),
442	                    )
443	                )
444	        return tuple(groups)

448	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
449	        """Load decision files -> capture -> query -> diff -> build review groups. Read-only.
450	
451	        Nothing here may mutate either machine: a job plans and reviews before it
452	        converges, so `plan()` runs before the user has approved anything. Both
453	        machines' decision files are loaded first (a read, like everything else here)
454	        and each side's captured/queried items are filtered through its OWN file before
455	        diffing (D-08): an item recorded on the source is dropped from the source
456	        manifest so it is never pushed to a peer again; an item recorded on the target
457	        is dropped from the target query so it is never proposed for
458	        install/remove/change again — either way it produces no `ItemDiff` and never
459	        reaches the review.
460	        """
461	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
462	        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
463	
464	        source_items = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
465	        target_items = await filter_inert(await self.query_target_items(), target_decisions)
466	        hold_pin_facts = await self.collect_hold_pin_facts()
467	        source_hold_names, target_hold_names = await self.collect_hold_sets()
468	        missing_item_ids = frozenset(item.item_id for item in source_items) - frozenset(
469	            item.item_id for item in target_items
470	        )
471	        unavailable_item_ids = await self.collect_unavailable_item_ids(missing_item_ids)
472	        diffs = self.diff_items(
473	            source_items,
474	            target_items,
475	            hold_pin_facts=hold_pin_facts,
476	            unavailable_item_ids=unavailable_item_ids,
477	            source_hold_names=source_hold_names,
478	            target_hold_names=target_hold_names,
479	        )
480	        groups = self._build_review_groups(diffs)
481	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=diffs, groups=groups)
482	
483	    def accept_review(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> None:
484	        """Store this job's plan plus the outcome its own review returned."""
485	        self._accepted_plan = plan
486	        self._accepted_outcome = outcome
487	
488	    async def after_review(self) -> None:
489	        """Hook: work that must run AFTER this job's review returns but BEFORE any
490	        mutation on the target (`apply()`).
491	
492	        No-op on the base — the three managers that produce no unreproducible items (apt,
493	        snap, flatpak) need nothing between review and converge. Only `manual_installs_sync`
494	        overrides it (D-23): it pushes the freshly reconciled install-snippet registry to
495	        the target here, so a snippet the user authored during THIS run's review is on the
496	        target before `apply()` replays it. Keeping the hook on the base leaves `execute()`
497	        the single source of the plan/review/apply order rather than each manager
498	        re-deriving it.
499	        """
500	        return
501	
502	    async def apply(self) -> None:
503	        """Converge every APPLY-decided diff from the accepted plan, one item at a time.
504	
505	        Per-item detail at `LogLevel.FULL`, one `LogLevel.INFO` summary line per job
506	        (ADR-010). A per-item failure (`ConvergeItemFailed`, or a converge command that
507	        exits non-zero) is caught, logged with its stderr as structured context, and
508	        collected — the loop always completes (D-27) — then `PackageItemFailures` is
509	        raised once, after the loop, if anything failed OR anything is left unresolved
510	        (D-21) — even when `total` is zero, since an interactive run whose ONLY diffs
511	        were unreproducible items never has any INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE work to do, and
512	        must still fail if one of them ended up unresolved.
513	
514	        Dry-run (ADR-014): each intended action is logged at FULL with a `[dry-run] `
515	        prefix and no converge command is ever issued.
516	
517	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs are excluded here regardless of decision: they imply no
518	        converge verb (D-25's held/pinned, version-mismatch, repo-unavailable,
519	        unreproducible classes are informational), so `converge()` is never called
520	        for one even if something recorded `APPLY` against it.
521	
522	        Before converging anything, `_record_permanent_skips` persists a `DecisionEntry`
523	        for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided item (D-08). The `_finalize_unreproducible` hook
524	        then persists this run's authored snippets and unreproducible-item skip-always
525	        decisions (D-20/D-21/D-23); it is a no-op on the base and only
526	        `manual_installs_sync` implements it (D-18), but the call site stays here so both
527	        run before any converge, independent of whether this run applies anything else
528	        (a run with zero installs but one newly-authored snippet still records it). The
529	        `_unresolved_as_failures` hook (also no-op on the base, overridden only by
530	        `manual_installs_sync`) supplies the genuinely-undecided items that fail an
531	        interactive run — which is why `total == 0` can still raise `PackageItemFailures`.
532	        """
533	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
534	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
535	        plan = self._accepted_plan
536	        outcome = self._accepted_outcome
537	        decisions = outcome.decisions
538	
539	        await self._record_permanent_skips(plan, decisions)
540	        await self._finalize_unreproducible(plan, outcome)
541	
542	        apply_diffs = [
543	            diff
544	            for diff in plan.diffs
545	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY and diff.action != DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
546	        ]
547	        prefix = "[dry-run] " if self.context.dry_run else ""
548	        total = len(apply_diffs)
549	
550	        failures: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]] = []
551	        if total == 0:
552	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}No {self.manager_id} changes to apply")
553	            self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=100))
554	        else:
555	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}Applying {total} {self.manager_id} change(s)")
556	
557	            for index, diff in enumerate(apply_diffs):
558	                if self.context.dry_run:
559	                    self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"{prefix}Would {diff.action.value} {diff.label}")
560	                else:
561	                    await self._converge_one(diff, failures)
562	                self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=int((index + 1) / total * 100)))
563	
564	            succeeded = total - len(failures)
565	            self._log(
566	                Host.TARGET,
567	                LogLevel.INFO,
568	                f"{prefix}{succeeded}/{total} {self.manager_id} change(s) applied",
569	            )
570	
571	        all_failures = [*failures, *self._unresolved_as_failures(plan, outcome)]
572	        if all_failures:
573	            summary = "; ".join(f"{diff.label}: {stderr.strip()}" for diff, stderr in all_failures)
574	            self._log(
575	                Host.TARGET,
576	                LogLevel.INFO,
577	                f"{len(all_failures)} {self.manager_id} item(s) failed: {summary}",
578	            )
579	            raise PackageItemFailures(self.manager_id, all_failures)
580	
581	    def _unresolved_as_failures(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]]:
582	        """Hook: this job's genuinely-undecided items that fail an interactive run (D-27).
583	
584	        No-op on the base — it returns an empty list, so the three managers that produce
585	        no unreproducible items (apt, snap, flatpak) never fail on this basis. Only
586	        `manual_installs_sync` overrides it (D-18/D-21): an unreproducible item left with
587	        neither a snippet nor a recorded decision after an interactive review fails the
588	        job. The D-27 converge-failure contract in `apply()` is unchanged — converge
589	        failures fail the job regardless of what this hook returns.
590	        """
591	        return []
592	
593	    async def _finalize_unreproducible(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> None:
594	        """Hook: persist this job's unreproducible-item snippet authoring and skip-always
595	        decisions (D-20/D-21/D-23).
596	
597	        No-op on the base — only `manual_installs_sync` produces unreproducible items
598	        (D-18), and it overrides this hook with the real persistence; the three managers
599	        that never do inherit this no-op so the base `apply()` stays generic.
600	        """
601	        return
602	
603	    async def _record_permanent_skips(self, plan: PackagePlan, decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]) -> None:
604	        """Persist a `DecisionEntry` for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided, actionable diff.
605	
606	        D-08a decides WHICH machine's file gets the entry by which machine HOLDS the
607	        item: `INSTALL`/`CHANGE` diffs are source-held (the source has the item, or the
608	        version it should converge to), so they record on `self.source`; `REMOVE` diffs
609	        are target-held (only the target has the item), so they record on `self.target`
610	        — through the remote executor, never a local write (ADR-002).
611	
612	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs are skipped: they carry no converge verb (version-mismatch,
613	        held/pinned, repo-unavailable, unreproducible are informational only), so there
614	        is no "holder" for D-08a to record against.
615	
616	        Two guards, both required before anything is ever written: never for a
617	        non-interactive outcome (D-26 — nothing is recorded permanently when nothing
618	        was actually decided by a human), and never during a dry run (ADR-014 — a
619	        rehearsal must leave no trace).
620	        """
621	        if self.context.dry_run or not self._accepted_outcome_was_interactive():
622	            return
623	
624	        recorded_at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
625	        for diff in plan.diffs:
626	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) != Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS:
627	                continue
628	            if diff.action not in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE, DiffAction.REMOVE):
629	                continue
630	
631	            executor = self.source if diff.action in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE) else self.target
632	            await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, executor).record(
633	                DecisionEntry(
634	                    item_id=diff.item_id,
635	                    item_class=diff.item_class,
636	                    label=diff.label,
637	                    reason=None,
638	                    recorded_at=recorded_at,
639	                )
640	            )
641	
642	    def _accepted_outcome_was_interactive(self) -> bool:
643	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
644	        return self._accepted_outcome.was_interactive
645	
646	    async def _converge_one(self, diff: ItemDiff, failures: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]]) -> None:
647	        try:
648	            result = await self.converge(diff)
649	        except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
650	            failures.append((diff, str(exc)))
651	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.ERROR, f"{diff.label} failed: {exc}", stderr=str(exc))
652	            return
653	
654	        if result.success:
655	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"{diff.action.value} {diff.label}")
656	        else:
657	            failures.append((diff, result.stderr))
658	            self._log(
659	                Host.TARGET,
660	                LogLevel.ERROR,
661	                f"{diff.label} failed: {result.stderr.strip()}",
662	                stderr=result.stderr,
663	            )

665	    async def execute(self) -> None:
666	        """The `SyncJob` entry point the orchestrator's sequential job loop calls.
667	
668	        Self-contained (D-24): plan this job's diffs, review its own groups through the
669	        injected `JobContext.reviewer`, accept the outcome, run the `after_review()` hook
670	        (the seam where `manual_installs_sync` pushes its snippet registry, D-23), then
671	        apply. No component outside the job owns its review, and no fallback applies diffs
672	        that never came back from one — a missing reviewer fails loudly here rather than
673	        silently skipping the review and converging unreviewed diffs (T-02-38).
674	
675	        A `plan()` failure propagates unchanged, so the orchestrator's per-job exception
676	        handling attributes it to this job's own `JobResult`.
677	        """
678	        assert self.context.reviewer is not None, (
679	            f"{self.manager_id} sync has no reviewer; the orchestrator must inject one "
680	            "through JobContext.reviewer before execute()."
681	        )
682	        plan = await self.plan()
683	        outcome = await self.context.reviewer.review(plan.groups)
684	        self.accept_review(plan, outcome)
685	        await self.after_review()
686	        await self.apply()

1	"""Batched checkbox review — the single interaction surface for every package diff (D-24).
2	
3	`apt_sync`, `snap_sync` and `flatpak_sync` (plans 02-06..02-11) each compute a set of
4	differences against the source's manifest and hand them to `review_items` as
5	`ReviewGroup`s before applying anything. The user ticks items off a checkable list in one
6	sitting rather than answering a sequence of yes/no prompts.
7	
8	This composes with the single persistent Live display (Phase 1 plans 01-17/01-18) exactly
9	as `TerminalUIConfirmer.confirm` (`pcswitcher.confirmer`) does: pause the live region before
10	the prompt, run the blocking `questionary` checkbox off the event loop via
11	`asyncio.to_thread` (ADR-005 — no blocking calls on the event loop), and resume it in a
12	`finally` so the terminal is always handed back even if the prompt raises.
13	
14	Removals get their own group, never sharing a checkbox list with installs (D-07/D-24): a
15	bulk tick that also deletes software would be exactly the silent-destruction failure D-07
16	exists to prevent. Which of a caller's `ReviewGroup`s are "removal-direction" is decided by
17	`ReviewGroup.action` — grouping itself (turning an `ItemDiff` into `ReviewGroup`s keyed by
18	manager+action) is Claude's Discretion for plan 02-05, which owns the real item model; this
19	module only consumes already-grouped input.
20	
21	`PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION_ENV`: undocumented escape hatch for integration tests, which run
22	without a TTY and cannot drive a real terminal prompt. When set, its value is trusted JSON
23	(no schema validation) mapping item_id -> decision, applied instead of prompting. It never
24	widens what the review offers (D-25 items are still exactly what the caller passed in) and
25	is deliberately absent from `--help`, the config schema and user docs (D-26).
26	
27	A `ReviewGroup` whose `action` is `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` gets a different
28	interaction shape from every other group (D-21): instead of a checkbox tick, each entry
29	is resolved one at a time with a three-way choice — add an install snippet, record it as
30	machine-specific (skip always), or skip for now — because "should this apply" is not the
31	question for an item no package manager can reproduce; "how does this get resolved" is.
32	`ReviewOutcome.snippets` carries that group's authored snippets back to the caller
33	(`PackageSyncJob.apply()`), which persists them. An interactive review always resolves
34	every entry (decision 10): an empty snippet capture re-prompts rather than falling through
35	to an "unresolved" state, and Ctrl-C / EOF anywhere in the review aborts the whole sync
36	(`SyncAbortedByUser`) rather than skipping items. `ReviewOutcome.unresolved` is therefore
37	populated only on the non-interactive path, where it reports (never fails) the items no
38	one was present to resolve (D-26).
39	
40	A `ReviewGroup` whose `action` is `COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION` likewise gets its own
41	interaction shape (D-30): each entry is a manually-installed package the pending apt
42	transaction would remove or downgrade, resolved one at a time with a three-way choice —
43	install anyway, skip, or abort. The decision is recorded against the entry's `item_id`
44	(the triggering install, set by the caller), so install-anyway proceeds with that install,
45	skip leaves it unapproved, and abort raises `SyncAbortedByUser` naming the collateral
46	package. A non-interactive run leaves every collateral entry `SKIP_ONCE` like every other
47	item, so the install it gates is simply not approved (D-26).
48	"""

238	async def _review_unreproducible_group(
239	    group: ReviewGroup,
240	    *,
241	    console: Console,
242	    decisions: dict[str, Decision],
243	    snippets: dict[str, str],
244	) -> None:
245	    """Resolve one `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` group's entries, one at a time, with
246	    the three-way choice D-21 requires: add an install snippet, record as
247	    machine-specific (skip always), or skip for now. Never a checkbox tick — a checkbox
248	    answers "should this apply", but an unreproducible item's question is "how does this
249	    get resolved", which is not a yes/no.
250	
251	    All three choices are VALID resolutions (D-21): a snippet, a skip-always, and an
252	    explicit skip-once. There is no fourth "genuinely undecided" outcome (decision 10 —
253	    unresolved must be unrepresentable in an interactive flow):
254	
255	    - Ctrl-C / EOF at the resolution choice (`select` returns `None`) means the user wants
256	      to stop, so it aborts the ENTIRE sync with `SyncAbortedByUser` — never a per-item
257	      skip-and-mark-unresolved.
258	    - Choosing "add an install snippet" and then submitting an empty body (or abandoning
259	      the editor) is NOT accepted and does NOT fall through: the three-way choice is
260	      re-prompted so the user must supply a real snippet or pick an explicit skip.
261	
262	    The body is stored verbatim, never stripped — D-20 forbids reasoning about it, and
263	    leading whitespace/newlines are the user's own formatting choice; "empty" means only a
264	    completely blank submission.
265	    """
266	    for entry in group.entries:
267	        console.print()
268	        console.print(Text(entry.label, style="bold"))
269	        if entry.detail:
270	            console.print(Text(entry.detail, style="dim"))
271	
272	        # Re-prompt until the entry is resolved by a real snippet or an explicit skip. An
273	        # empty snippet capture loops back here rather than manufacturing an unresolved
274	        # item (decision 10); a cancelled choice breaks out by aborting the whole sync.
275	        while True:
276	            choice_prompt = questionary.select(
277	                f"How should {entry.label} be resolved?",
278	                choices=[
279	                    questionary.Choice(title="Add an install snippet", value="add_snippet"),
280	                    questionary.Choice(title="Record as machine-specific (skip always)", value="skip_always"),
281	                    questionary.Choice(title="Skip for now", value="skip_once"),
282	                ],
283	            )
284	            selected = await asyncio.to_thread(choice_prompt.ask)
285	
286	            if selected is None:
287	                # Ctrl-C / EOF: the user wants to abort, not skip this one item (decision
288	                # 10). Raise the clean-stop control-flow exception the orchestrator and CLI
289	                # already catch once at WARNING, so the whole sync stops here.
290	                raise SyncAbortedByUser(
291	                    f"package review aborted while resolving unreproducible item {entry.label!r} (Ctrl-C/EOF)"
292	                )
293	
294	            if selected == "skip_always":
295	                decisions[entry.item_id] = Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS
296	                break
297	
298	            if selected == "skip_once":
299	                # An explicit "Skip for now" is a real decision (D-21): the item is
300	                # resolved for this run.
301	                decisions[entry.item_id] = Decision.SKIP_ONCE
302	                break
303	
304	            # selected == "add_snippet"
305	            console.print(Text(_SNIPPET_AUTHORING_NOTE, style="dim"))
306	            body_prompt = questionary.text(
307	                f"Install snippet for {entry.label} (Esc then Enter to finish):", multiline=True
308	            )
309	            body = await asyncio.to_thread(body_prompt.ask)
310	            if body:
311	                snippets[entry.item_id] = body
312	                break
313	
314	            # Empty submission or an abandoned editor (`""`/`None`): not a resolution and
315	            # not an unresolved fall-through — re-prompt the three-way choice (decision 10).
316	            console.print(
317	                Text("An install snippet cannot be empty — enter a real snippet or choose a skip.", style="yellow")
318	            )

321	async def _review_collateral_group(
322	    group: ReviewGroup,
323	    *,
324	    console: Console,
325	    decisions: dict[str, Decision],
326	) -> None:
327	    """Resolve one `COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION` group's entries, one at a time, with the
328	    three-way choice D-30 requires for a manually-installed package the pending apt
329	    transaction would remove or downgrade: install anyway, skip, or abort. Never a
330	    checkbox tick — losing a package the user chose to have is not the same yes/no as
331	    ticking an install off a list.
332	
333	    The decision is recorded against `entry.item_id`: install-anyway records
334	    `Decision.APPLY`, skip records `Decision.SKIP_ONCE`. The caller (`AptSyncJob`) maps
335	    that onto the triggering install — APPLY lets the install proceed and allows the
336	    collateral removal, SKIP_ONCE leaves the install unapproved so the collateral is not
337	    removed. Abort raises `SyncAbortedByUser` — the existing user-decline control-flow
338	    exception, caught once at WARNING by both the orchestrator and the CLI — naming the
339	    collateral package, so the whole run stops cleanly rather than applying a transaction
340	    the user did not accept.
341	
342	    Every untrusted label/detail is wrapped in `Text` before it reaches the console, so a
343	    package name containing bracket characters cannot trigger the Rich markup crash the
344	    phase already guards against (T-02-02).
345	    """
346	    for entry in group.entries:
347	        console.print()
348	        console.print(Text(entry.label, style="bold"))
349	        if entry.detail:
350	            console.print(Text(entry.detail, style="dim"))
351	
352	        choice_prompt = questionary.select(
353	            f"{entry.label} is manually installed and would be removed or downgraded. Proceed?",
354	            choices=[
355	                questionary.Choice(title="Install anyway (allow the collateral removal)", value="install_anyway"),
356	                questionary.Choice(title="Skip (leave the triggering install unapproved)", value="skip"),
357	                questionary.Choice(title="Abort the sync", value="abort"),
358	            ],
359	        )
360	        selected = await asyncio.to_thread(choice_prompt.ask)
361	
362	        if selected == "install_anyway":
363	            decisions[entry.item_id] = Decision.APPLY
364	        elif selected == "abort":
365	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(
366	                f"collateral removal of manually-installed {entry.label} declined (abort chosen in review)"
367	            )
368	        else:
369	            # "skip", None (the select was cancelled): leave the triggering install
370	            # unapproved for this run, so the collateral is not removed.
371	            decisions[entry.item_id] = Decision.SKIP_ONCE

374	async def review_items(
375	    groups: Sequence[ReviewGroup],
376	    *,
377	    console: Console,
378	    ui: PausableUI,
379	    logger: logging.Logger | None = None,
380	) -> ReviewOutcome:
381	    """Present every group as a checkable list and return the user's decisions.
382	
383	    Non-interactive runs (`is_interactive(console)` is False) prompt for nothing: every
384	    item comes back `SKIP_ONCE`, nothing is recorded permanently, and a warning names how
385	    many items went unresolved (D-26). Interactive runs pause `ui` around each group's
386	    blocking `questionary` checkbox (dispatched via `asyncio.to_thread`) and resume it in
387	    a `finally`, so the live display is always handed back even if the prompt raises.
388	    """
389	    log = logger if logger is not None else _logger
390	
391	    automation_raw = os.environ.get(PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION_ENV)
392	    if automation_raw is not None:
393	        return ReviewOutcome(decisions=_decisions_from_automation(groups, automation_raw), was_interactive=True)
394	
395	    if not is_interactive(console):
396	        total = sum(len(group.entries) for group in groups)
397	        log.warning("%d package review item(s) left unresolved (non-interactive run)", total)
398	        for group in groups:
399	            console.print(_render_group_panel(group))
400	        decisions = {entry.item_id: Decision.SKIP_ONCE for group in groups for entry in group.entries}
401	        # D-26: no capture is ever offered without a TTY, so every unreproducible item
402	        # is unresolved by construction — never a snippet, never a recorded decision.
403	        non_interactive_unresolved = tuple(
404	            entry.item_id for group in groups if _is_unreproducible_group(group.action) for entry in group.entries
405	        )
406	        return ReviewOutcome(decisions=decisions, was_interactive=False, unresolved=non_interactive_unresolved)
407	
408	    ui.pause()
409	    decisions: dict[str, Decision] = {}
410	    snippets: dict[str, str] = {}
411	    try:
412	        for group in groups:
413	            console.print()
414	            console.print(_render_group_panel(group))
415	
416	            if _is_unreproducible_group(group.action):
417	                await _review_unreproducible_group(group, console=console, decisions=decisions, snippets=snippets)
418	                continue
419	
420	            if _is_collateral_group(group.action):
421	                await _review_collateral_group(group, console=console, decisions=decisions)
422	                continue
423	
424	            removal = _is_removal_direction(group.action)
425	            choices = [
426	                questionary.Choice(
427	                    title=f"{entry.action_label} {entry.label}",
428	                    value=entry.item_id,
429	                    checked=not removal,
430	                )
431	                for entry in group.entries
432	            ]
433	            prompt = questionary.checkbox(group.title, choices=choices)
434	            selected = await asyncio.to_thread(prompt.ask)
435	
436	            if selected is None:
437	                # Ctrl-C / EOF at a checkbox screen means the user wants to abort, not
438	                # silently skip the rest of the review (decision 10). Raise the clean-stop
439	                # control-flow exception so the whole sync stops here rather than leaving
440	                # this and every later group's items undecided.
441	                raise SyncAbortedByUser("package review aborted at a checkbox screen (Ctrl-C/EOF)")
442	
443	            selected_ids = set(selected)
444	            for entry in group.entries:
445	                decisions[entry.item_id] = Decision.APPLY if entry.item_id in selected_ids else Decision.SKIP_ONCE
446	    finally:
447	        ui.resume()
448	
449	    # An interactive review can no longer leave anything unresolved (decision 10): the
450	    # unreproducible flow re-prompts or aborts, and a checkbox abort raises above — so
451	    # `unresolved` is always empty here. It stays populated only on the non-interactive
452	    # path (D-26 reporting).
453	    return ReviewOutcome(decisions=decisions, was_interactive=True, snippets=snippets, unresolved=())

1	"""Machine-local decision store: the ONLY pc-switcher state deliberately per-machine
2	and never synced (D-08, D-08a, D-09).
3	
4	An entry recorded here means "inert on THIS machine in both roles": not pushed when
5	this machine is the source, not installed or removed when this machine is the target.
6	D-19's whole argument for scanning aggressively — a finding produces noise exactly
7	once, then never again — only holds if this durability is real.
8	
9	Which machine's file gets an entry follows which machine HOLDS the item (D-08a): a
10	source-held item declined during review is recorded on the source, a target-held
11	item whose removal is declined is recorded on the target. Because the file is
12	machine-local, the write must land on the correct END of the connection — on the
13	target this means going through the remote executor, never a local `pathlib` write
14	(ADR-002: the target has no direct filesystem access from here). `DecisionFile` takes
15	an `Executor` at construction and issues every read/write as a shell command through
16	it, so the SAME code path serves both roles; there is no separate "local write"
17	branch to accidentally use for the target.
18	
19	Decision files live at `~/.config/pc-switcher/<manager>.decisions.yaml`, next to
20	`config.yaml` (D-09) — one file per manager, so `apt_sync`'s decisions never collide
21	with `snap_sync`'s. The directory portion is derived from `config_sync.CONFIG_REMOTE_DIR`
22	rather than a second hardcoded literal (the CR-01 precedent `folder_sync` already
23	follows for its own tool-state filter token).
24	
25	This module also owns `SnippetRegistry` (D-20, D-23): the SHARED, synced counterpart to
26	the machine-local decision store above. Where a `DecisionEntry` says "never touch this
27	item on this machine", a `Snippet` says "this is how to install something no package
28	manager can reproduce" — knowledge about the PACKAGE, not the machine, so it is SHARED
29	and synced (D-23) rather than living in a machine-local `*.decisions.yaml` file. It
30	travels source-to-target by `manual_installs_sync`'s own post-review `send_file` push,
31	not via `config_sync`. A snippet's body is stored and replayed as an opaque text
32	blob — never parsed, versioned, diffed or reasoned about (D-20) — and replay never
33	supplies stdin, since `pcswitcher.executor.Process` documents that commands must be
34	non-interactive; a snippet expecting a prompt fails rather than hanging the sync.
35	"""

100	class DecisionEntry:
101	    """One permanent "skip always" decision (D-07's third outcome), persisted by
102	    `DecisionFile.record` and read back by `DecisionFile.load`.
103	    """
104	
105	    item_id: str

117	async def filter_inert[T: _HasItemId](items: Sequence[T], decisions: Mapping[str, DecisionEntry]) -> list[T]:
118	    """Items whose `item_id` is ABSENT from `decisions` — the ones still live.
119	
120	    A pure, module-level function (not a method) so both the source-capture side
121	    (drop recorded items from the manifest before it is even diffed) and the
122	    target-query side (drop recorded items from what would otherwise become a
123	    proposed install/remove) share exactly one definition of "inert" (D-08).
124	    """
125	    return [item for item in items if item.item_id not in decisions]

128	def _serialize(entries: Mapping[str, DecisionEntry]) -> str:
129	    """Render `entries` as the decision-file YAML body, header regenerated fresh."""
130	    machine_specific = {
131	        item_id: {
132	            "item_class": entry.item_class.value,
133	            "label": entry.label,
134	            "reason": entry.reason,
135	            "recorded_at": entry.recorded_at,
136	        }
137	        for item_id, entry in entries.items()
138	    }
139	    body = yaml.safe_dump({"machine_specific": machine_specific}, sort_keys=False, default_flow_style=False)
140	    return f"{_FILE_HEADER}\n{body}"

143	def _deserialize(raw: str) -> dict[str, DecisionEntry]:
144	    """Parse a decision file's content into `{item_id: DecisionEntry}`.
145	
146	    Raises on anything that isn't the expected shape; callers translate that into
147	    the "no permanent decisions" empty-mapping fallback (see `DecisionFile.load`).
148	    """
149	    data = yaml.safe_load(raw)
150	    machine_specific = data.get("machine_specific") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
151	    if not isinstance(machine_specific, dict):
152	        raise ValueError("decision file has no 'machine_specific' mapping")
153	
154	    entries: dict[str, DecisionEntry] = {}
155	    for item_id, fields in machine_specific.items():
156	        entries[str(item_id)] = DecisionEntry(
157	            item_id=str(item_id),
158	            item_class=ItemClass(fields["item_class"]),
159	            label=fields["label"],
160	            reason=fields.get("reason"),
161	            recorded_at=fields["recorded_at"],
162	        )
163	    return entries

166	class DecisionFile:
167	    """Read/write access to ONE manager's machine-local decision file, through
168	    whichever `Executor` is local to the machine that should hold it (D-08a).
169	
170	    Construct with `executor=self.source` to read/write the SOURCE machine's file,
171	    or `executor=self.target` to read/write the TARGET machine's file — the caller
172	    (`PackageSyncJob`, plan 02-04 task 2) decides which per D-08a, this class only
173	    ever talks to the executor it was given.
174	    """
175	
176	    def __init__(self, manager: str, executor: Executor) -> None:
177	        self._manager = manager
178	        self._executor = executor
179	        # shlex.quote() is a no-op for this fixed, already-shell-safe relpath (only
180	        # word chars, '.', '/'), but is applied anyway per T-02-01 (ASVS V5) rather
181	        # than assuming a future manager name stays that safe. Left OUTSIDE the `~/`
182	        # prefix: quoting the whole `~/...` expression would disable tilde expansion,
183	        # while `~/` immediately followed by a (possibly-)quoted word is still one
184	        # shell word — bash expands the leading `~/` and appends the rest literally.
185	        relpath = DECISION_FILE_RELPATH_TEMPLATE.format(manager=manager)
186	        self._path_expr = f"~/{shlex.quote(relpath)}"
187	        self._display_path = f"~/{relpath}"
188	
189	    async def load(self) -> dict[str, DecisionEntry]:
190	        """Read this manager's decisions, or an empty mapping (D-08's degrade rule).
191	
192	        Absent, empty and malformed all degrade to "no permanent decisions" rather
193	        than aborting the sync; only the malformed case logs a WARNING (naming the
194	        path) since that one indicates the file was tampered with or hand-edited
195	        incorrectly, not simply "nothing recorded yet".
196	        """
197	        result = await self._executor.run_command(f"cat {self._path_expr} 2>/dev/null")
198	        if not result.success or not result.stdout.strip():
199	            return {}
200	
201	        try:
202	            return _deserialize(result.stdout)
203	        except (yaml.YAMLError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
204	            _logger.warning(
205	                "Malformed decision file %s (%s); treating as no permanent decisions",
206	                self._display_path,
207	                exc,
208	            )
209	            return {}
210	
211	    async def record(self, entry: DecisionEntry) -> None:
212	        """Merge `entry` into this file by `item_id` (last write wins) and write
213	        atomically: `mkdir -p` the directory, write the new content to a sibling
214	        `.pcswitcher-tmp` path, then `mv -f` it into place — the same
215	        atomic-replace-within-the-same-directory shape `vscode_state_sync._sync_editor`
216	        uses, so an interrupted write can never leave a truncated file.
217	
218	        The serialised bytes travel as one shlex-quoted `printf` argument through
219	        `self._executor` — never a local filesystem write — so this identical method
220	        is correct whether `self._executor` is the source's `LocalExecutor` or the
221	        target's `RemoteExecutor`.
222	        """
223	        entries = await self.load()
224	        entries[entry.item_id] = entry
225	        content = _serialize(entries)
226	
227	        dir_relpath = shlex.quote(_DECISION_DIR_RELPATH)
228	        tmp_expr = f"{self._path_expr}.pcswitcher-tmp"
229	        cmd = (
230	            f"mkdir -p ~/{dir_relpath} && "
231	            f"printf '%s' {shlex.quote(content)} > {tmp_expr} && "
232	            f"mv -f {tmp_expr} {self._path_expr}"
233	        )
234	        result = await self._executor.run_command(
235	            cmd, mutates=f"record permanent skip for {entry.label} in {self._display_path}"
236	        )
237	        if not result.success:
238	            raise RuntimeError(
239	                f"failed to record decision for {entry.item_id!r} in {self._display_path}: {result.stderr.strip()}"
240	            )

251	    "# an item no package manager can reproduce (D-20): a bare .deb or a manual\n"
252	    "# install. The tool never parses, versions, diffs or reasons about the body —\n"
253	    "# edit or remove an entry by hand if it goes stale.\n"
254	    "#\n"
255	    "# This file lives in the shared, synced config (D-23): every peer that runs\n"
256	    "# `pc-switcher sync` carries it to the target alongside config.yaml. A snippet\n"
257	    "# replays non-interactively with no stdin available — one that expects a prompt\n"
258	    "# fails rather than hanging the sync.\n"

262	@dataclass(frozen=True)
263	class Snippet:
264	    """One recorded install snippet (D-20): an opaque shell command that reproduces an
265	    item no package manager can install on its own.
266	
267	    `label` mirrors the unreproducible item's own label at authoring time (a snapshot,
268	    not a live reference) so the registry file reads meaningfully on its own. `body` is
269	    NEVER inspected by this dataclass or its callers beyond being replayed byte-for-byte.
270	    """
271	
272	    item_id: str
273	    label: str
274	    body: str
275	    authored_at: str  # ISO-8601 UTC
276	    authored_on: str  # hostname of the machine the snippet was authored on
277	
278	
279	def _serialize_snippets(entries: Mapping[str, Snippet]) -> str:
280	    """Render `entries` as the snippet-registry YAML body, header regenerated fresh."""
281	    snippets = {
282	        item_id: {
283	            "label": entry.label,
284	            "body": entry.body,
285	            "authored_at": entry.authored_at,
286	            "authored_on": entry.authored_on,
287	        }
288	        for item_id, entry in entries.items()
289	    }
290	    body = yaml.safe_dump({"snippets": snippets}, sort_keys=False, default_flow_style=False)
291	    return f"{_SNIPPET_FILE_HEADER}\n{body}"
292	
293	
294	def _deserialize_snippets(raw: str) -> dict[str, Snippet]:
295	    """Parse a snippet registry's content into `{item_id: Snippet}`.
296	
297	    Raises on anything that isn't the expected shape; callers translate that into
298	    the "no snippets" empty-mapping fallback (see `SnippetRegistry.load`).
299	    """
300	    data = yaml.safe_load(raw)
301	    snippets = data.get("snippets") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
302	    if not isinstance(snippets, dict):
303	        raise ValueError("snippet registry has no 'snippets' mapping")
304	
305	    entries: dict[str, Snippet] = {}
306	    for item_id, fields in snippets.items():
307	        entries[str(item_id)] = Snippet(
308	            item_id=str(item_id),
309	            label=fields["label"],
310	            body=fields["body"],
311	            authored_at=fields["authored_at"],
312	            authored_on=fields["authored_on"],
313	        )
314	    return entries

317	def load_snippets_from_text(raw: str) -> dict[str, Snippet]:
318	    """Parse snippet-registry file content into `{item_id: Snippet}`, degrading to an
319	    empty mapping on empty or malformed input (the same rule `SnippetRegistry.load`
320	    applies to executor-read content).
321	
322	    `manual_installs_sync` uses this to read the SOURCE's on-disk registry — the exact
323	    bytes `_push_snippet_registry` is about to `send_file` to the target — when deciding
324	    whether a wholesale overwrite is purely additive (decision 9). Reading the file that
325	    is actually sent keeps the additive check consistent with the transfer, rather than
326	    re-querying the source executor which may lag the just-finalized on-disk file.
327	    """
328	    if not raw.strip():
329	        return {}
330	    try:
331	        return _deserialize_snippets(raw)
332	    except (yaml.YAMLError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
333	        _logger.warning("Malformed snippet registry (%s); treating as no snippets", exc)
334	        return {}

337	class SnippetRegistry:
338	    """Read/write/replay access to the shared install-snippet registry, through
339	    whichever `Executor` is local to the machine this instance should read/write
340	    (same one-`Executor`-per-instance shape `DecisionFile` follows).
341	
342	    Unlike `DecisionFile`, the registry is not machine-scoped data — both machines may
343	    hold different copies of the SAME file until `manual_installs_sync` reconciles them
344	    by pushing the source's copy to the target (D-23). Construct with
345	    `SnippetRegistry(self.source)` to read/write the source's own copy — the reproducibility
346	    authority `plan()` classifies against (corrected D-23), and where a freshly authored
347	    snippet is recorded before that run's push carries it to the target — or
348	    `SnippetRegistry(self.target)` to read the target's copy at converge time, after this
349	    run's push has already placed it there.
350	    """
351	
352	    def __init__(self, executor: Executor) -> None:
353	        self._executor = executor
354	        # shlex.quote() is a no-op for this fixed, already-shell-safe relpath, applied
355	        # anyway per T-02-01 (ASVS V5) — see `DecisionFile.__init__`'s identical
356	        # reasoning for why it stays OUTSIDE the `~/` prefix.
357	        self._path_expr = f"~/{shlex.quote(SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH)}"
358	        self._display_path = f"~/{SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH}"
359	
360	    async def load(self) -> dict[str, Snippet]:
361	        """Read every snippet, or an empty mapping if the registry is absent, empty or
362	        malformed — mirrors `DecisionFile.load`'s degrade rule; only the malformed case
363	        logs a WARNING naming the path.
364	        """
365	        result = await self._executor.run_command(f"cat {self._path_expr} 2>/dev/null")
366	        if not result.success or not result.stdout.strip():
367	            return {}
368	
369	        try:
370	            return _deserialize_snippets(result.stdout)
371	        except (yaml.YAMLError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
372	            _logger.warning(
373	                "Malformed snippet registry %s (%s); treating as no snippets",
374	                self._display_path,
375	                exc,
376	            )
377	            return {}
378	
379	    async def get(self, item_id: str) -> Snippet | None:
380	        """The snippet registered for `item_id`, or `None` if there is none."""
381	        entries = await self.load()
382	        return entries.get(item_id)
383	
384	    async def add(self, snippet: Snippet) -> None:
385	        """Merge `snippet` into the registry by `item_id` (last write wins) and write
386	        atomically — the identical `mkdir -p && printf ... > tmp && mv -f` shape
387	        `DecisionFile.record` uses, so an interrupted write can never leave a truncated
388	        file.
389	        """
390	        entries = await self.load()
391	        entries[snippet.item_id] = snippet
392	        content = _serialize_snippets(entries)
393	
394	        dir_relpath = shlex.quote(_DECISION_DIR_RELPATH)
395	        tmp_expr = f"{self._path_expr}.pcswitcher-tmp"
396	        cmd = (
397	            f"mkdir -p ~/{dir_relpath} && "
398	            f"printf '%s' {shlex.quote(content)} > {tmp_expr} && "
399	            f"mv -f {tmp_expr} {self._path_expr}"
400	        )
401	        result = await self._executor.run_command(
402	            cmd, mutates=f"record install snippet for {snippet.label} in {self._display_path}"
403	        )
404	        if not result.success:
405	            raise RuntimeError(
406	                f"failed to add snippet for {snippet.item_id!r} in {self._display_path}: {result.stderr.strip()}"
407	            )
408	
409	    async def replay(self, item_id: str, executor: RemoteExecutor) -> CommandResult:
410	        """Replay the snippet registered for `item_id` against `executor` (always the
411	        TARGET in practice) as an opaque blob (D-20): the body is never parsed,
412	        templated or inspected, only quoted.
413	
414	        Runs as `bash -c <shlex.quote(body)>` — the same build-a-command,
415	        pass-content-as-an-argv-quoted-string shape `vscode_state_sync.target_sql_command`
416	        uses for SQL — with `login_shell=False`, since a snippet is a fixed shell script,
417	        not something that needs the user's `~/.profile` sourced. No stdin is ever
418	        supplied (`pcswitcher.executor.Process` documents this is intentional), so a
419	        snippet expecting a prompt fails rather than hanging the sync. The returned
420	        `CommandResult`'s exit code alone decides success — never raises for "no
421	        snippet registered", instead returning a failed `CommandResult` so a stale plan
422	        (the registry changed between `plan()` and `apply()`) is a per-item failure
423	        like any other, not a crash that stops the whole job (D-27).
424	
425	        The exact `bash -c <quoted body>` command is what `--confirm-each-command` shows:
426	        an opaque snippet is the one thing in a sync whose content pc-switcher cannot vouch
427	        for, so it is displayed verbatim before it runs.
428	        """
429	        snippet = await self.get(item_id)
430	        if snippet is None:
431	            return CommandResult(exit_code=1, stdout="", stderr=f"no snippet registered for {item_id!r}")
432	
433	        cmd = f"bash -c {shlex.quote(snippet.body)}"
434	        return await executor.run_command(
435	            cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"replay install snippet for {snippet.label}"
436	        )

4	Captures the source's `apt-mark showmanual` set with `dpkg-query`-sourced versions
5	(never `apt list --installed` — its own manpage says the output has no stable scripting
6	contract), diffs it against the same query on the target into every D-25 class
7	(`PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_packages`), and converges the approved `INSTALL`/`REMOVE`
8	items via `apt-get install`/`apt-get remove`.

11	command runs, guarding against apt silently doing more than the review showed. Collateral
12	effects are classified by provenance (D-30): a package the simulation would remove or

15	something the user chose to have and is refused unless the user approved losing it. `plan()`

17	set — not one per-package, which would cost more than the sync itself for 150 packages) and
18	classifies their collateral against the target manual set, emitting a three-way

171	# -- Repository/key/pin/config capture and diff (D-11, D-12, D-13) ---------------------
172	#
173	# Unlike apt packages, these five directories are diffed by whole-FILE digest (module
174	# docstring, RESEARCH's alternatives table): one batched `sha256sum` listing per
175	# directory tells us which filenames differ without transferring a single byte, and the
176	# full content of a file is only fetched for the files a diff actually implicates
177	# (missing-on-target, extra-on-target, or digest-mismatched) — never for a file that is
178	# already identical on both machines.
179	
180	_SIGNED_BY_RE = re.compile(r"^Signed-By:\s*(?P<path>\S+)", re.IGNORECASE)
181	_LEGACY_SIGNED_BY_RE = re.compile(r"signed-by=(?P<path>[^\]\s,]+)")
182	_PIN_PACKAGE_RE = re.compile(r"^Package:\s*(?P<packages>.+)$", re.IGNORECASE)

185	def _parse_sha256sum(output: str) -> dict[str, str]:
186	    """`<digest>  <path>` lines (one per `sha256sum` invocation) -> `{basename: digest}`.
187	
188	    Basename, not the full path: every caller already knows which directory it asked
189	    about, and item identity is the filename (module docstring), not the path.
190	    """
191	    digests: dict[str, str] = {}
192	    for line in _lines(output):
193	        parts = line.split(None, 1)
194	        if len(parts) != 2:
195	            continue
196	        digest, path = parts
197	        digests[Path(path).name] = digest
198	    return digests

201	def _parse_source_file(filename: str, content: str) -> tuple[Literal["deb822", "list"], tuple[str, ...]]:

204	    deb822 `.sources` files name a key via a `Signed-By:` field; legacy `.list` files
205	    name one inside the options bracket as `[... signed-by=<path> ...]` (RESEARCH
206	    Standard Stack). Parsed just far enough to extract these — never rewritten,
207	    normalised, or migrated between formats (RESEARCH Pitfall 3, deferred ideas).
208	    """
209	    fmt: Literal["deb822", "list"] = "deb822" if filename.endswith(".sources") else "list"
210	    refs: list[str] = []
211	    for line in content.splitlines():
212	        match = _SIGNED_BY_RE.match(line.strip()) if fmt == "deb822" else _LEGACY_SIGNED_BY_RE.search(line)
213	        if match:
214	            refs.append(match.group("path"))

245	async def _capture_dir_digests(run: Callable[[str], Awaitable[CommandResult]], directory: str) -> dict[str, str]:
246	    """One `sudo find <dir> -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec sha256sum {} +` per directory —
247	    a single batched command, never one `sha256sum` per file. `-exec ... {} +` never
248	    runs at all when the directory has no matching files, so an empty/absent directory
249	    degrades to an empty digest map rather than a shell error.

418	@dataclass(frozen=True)
419	class AptTransactionPreview:
420	    """The parsed result of `apt-get -s <args>` — what apt says it WOULD do.
421	
422	    `apt-get -s` is the only honest answer to "what will this command do": apt resolves
423	    dependencies and conflicts at run time, so the package the user ticked and the
424	    transaction apt actually runs are not necessarily the same thing.
425	
426	    `install_versions` maps a package apt would `Inst` to `(currently_installed_version
427	    | None, candidate_version)` — the currently-installed version is `None` for a fresh
428	    install (no `[...]` bracket in the line), present for an upgrade/downgrade. This is
429	    what the downgrade guard compares via `compare_deb_versions` rather than assuming
430	    every `Inst` line is a new install.
431	    """
432	
433	    installs: tuple[str, ...]
434	    removals: tuple[str, ...]
435	    raw: str
436	    install_versions: Mapping[str, tuple[str | None, str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
437	
438	
439	async def simulate_apt_transaction(
440	    executor: RemoteExecutor, apt_args: str, *, login_shell: bool | None = False
441	) -> AptTransactionPreview:
442	    """Run `apt-get -s <apt_args>` on `executor` and parse its Inst/Remv action lines.
443	
444	    No `sudo` is needed: simulation is read-only. Raises `ConvergeItemFailed` if the
445	    simulation itself fails (dpkg lock contention, unmet dependencies, a transient
446	    apt-cache read error): a failed `apt-get -s` typically prints no Inst/Remv lines,
447	    which would otherwise parse as an indistinguishable-from-clean empty preview and
448	    let both call sites proceed with a real command whose simulation was never
449	    actually trustworthy (WR-01) — refuse rather than silently degrade.
450	    """
451	    result = await executor.run_command(f"apt-get -s {apt_args}", login_shell=login_shell)
452	    if not result.success:
453	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"apt-get -s {apt_args} failed: {result.stderr.strip()}")
454	    installs: list[str] = []
455	    removals: list[str] = []
456	    install_versions: dict[str, tuple[str | None, str]] = {}
457	    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
458	        match = _TRANSACTION_LINE_RE.match(line)
459	        if match is None:
460	            continue
461	        verb, name = match.group("verb"), match.group("name")
462	        if verb == "Inst":
463	            installs.append(name)
464	            new_version = match.group("new_version")
465	            if new_version is not None:
466	                install_versions[name] = (match.group("old_version"), new_version)
467	        elif verb == "Remv":
468	            removals.append(name)
469	    return AptTransactionPreview(
470	        installs=tuple(installs), removals=tuple(removals), raw=result.stdout, install_versions=install_versions
471	    )

561	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[AptPackageItem]:
562	        """The target's own manually-installed apt packages, with versions."""
563	        manual = await self.target.run_command("apt-mark showmanual", login_shell=False)
564

570	    @staticmethod
571	    async def _resolve_versions(
572	        showmanual_output: str, run: Callable[[str], Awaitable[CommandResult]]
573	    ) -> list[AptPackageItem]:
574	        """Resolve every name's version with ONE `dpkg-query` call (RESEARCH.md)."""
575	        names = _lines(showmanual_output)
576	        if not names:
577	            return []
578	
579	        quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(name) for name in names)
580	        # dpkg-query, not `apt list --installed`: apt's own manpage warns the latter's
581	        # output has no stable contract for scripting. The literal \t/\n below are
582	        # dpkg-query's OWN format-string escapes (interpreted by dpkg-query, not the
583	        # shell) — hence a plain (non-f) string so Python leaves them as two-char
584	        # backslash sequences for dpkg-query to expand into real tab/newline.
585	        versions_result = await run("dpkg-query -W -f='${Package}\\t${Version}\\n' " + quoted)
586	
587	        versions: dict[str, str] = {}
588	        for line in versions_result.stdout.splitlines():
589	            if not line.strip():
590	                continue
591	            pkg_name, _, version = line.partition("\t")
592	            versions[pkg_name] = version
593	
594	        return [AptPackageItem(name=name, version=versions.get(name, "")) for name in names]

596	    @override
597	    async def collect_hold_pin_facts(self) -> Sequence[HoldPinFact]:
598	        """PIN facts from the target's `/etc/apt/preferences.d/*` `Package:` stanzas —
599	        the target-only `HELD_OR_PINNED`/`REPORT_ONLY` echo on the package item.
600	
601	        As of #208 this reads PINS only. HOLDS moved out of this hook: a hold is dpkg
602	        selection state (`apt-mark showhold`) replicated as its own `apt:hold:` membership
603	        item via `collect_hold_sets`, not surfaced as a package-level report — so a held
604	        package is never double-reported (once here and once as a hold item). A pin
605	        remains an apt priority preference that can still permit an upgrade, so it stays a
606	        report on the package rather than a converge action (RESEARCH Pitfall 2).
607	        """
608	        facts: list[HoldPinFact] = []
609	
610	        # `find ... -exec ... {} +` passes every matching file to one awk invocation
611	        # (not a per-file command); if the directory has no files, -exec never runs,
612	        # so an empty preferences.d produces empty output rather than a shell error.
613	        pins = await self.target.run_command(
614	            "find /etc/apt/preferences.d -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec awk '/^Package:/{print FILENAME \"\\t\" $2}' {} +",
615	            login_shell=False,
616	        )
617	        for line in _lines(pins.stdout):
618	            filename, _, package = line.partition("\t")
619	            if package:
620	                facts.append(HoldPinFact(mechanism="pin", package=package, source_ref=filename))
621	
622	        return facts

651	    @override
652	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
653	        """Extends the base diff (missing/extra/mismatch/held/unavailable) with

655	        `/etc/apt/*` repository item classes (D-11/D-12/D-13).
656	
657	        Unreproducible detection is NOT apt's business (D-18): it moved to
658	        `manual_installs_sync` with its own enable flag, so this job never emits an
659	        `UNREPRODUCIBLE` diff.
660	
661	        Runs AFTER the base diff and BEFORE review groups are (re)built. The batched
662	        apt-get -s simulations reveal what the pending transaction would also remove or
663	        downgrade; each such package is split by provenance against the target's
664	        `apt-mark showmanual` set (captured here, once). An auto-installed collateral
665	        package is apt resolving its own dependencies — it proceeds silently, producing no
666	        review item. A manually-installed collateral package is something the user chose to
667	        have, so it becomes its own three-way review item (install-anyway / skip / abort)
668	        decided at plan time, in the SAME review the user approves from — never a prompt
669	        during apply.
670	        """
671	        base_plan = await super().plan()
672	        self._target_manual_set = await self._capture_target_manual_set()
673	        collateral_diffs = await self._collect_plan_time_collateral(base_plan.diffs)
674	        repo_diffs = await self._plan_repo_diffs()
675	
676	        if not collateral_diffs and not repo_diffs:
677	            return base_plan
678	
679	        # Ordering is an apt FACT (key before source before packages, T-02-16), not a
680	        # general one: the base loop stays a plain item-by-item iterator, and THIS job
681	        # sorts its own diffs before they reach it. `sorted` is stable, so within one
682	        # rank (e.g. every APT_PACKAGE diff, or every APT_PIN/APT_CONFIG diff) the
683	        # original relative order — base diff, then collateral, then repo diffs — is
684	        # preserved.
685	        all_diffs = tuple(
686	            sorted(
687	                (*base_plan.diffs, *collateral_diffs, *repo_diffs),
688	                key=lambda diff: _ITEM_CLASS_ORDER.get(diff.item_class, 3),
689	            )
690	        )
691	        groups = self._build_review_groups(all_diffs)
692	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=all_diffs, groups=groups)

694	    @override
695	    def _build_review_groups(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> tuple[ReviewGroup, ...]:

697	        `COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION` group whose entries take the three-way install-anyway /
698	        skip / abort resolution, presented after the base groups (installs/changes/
699	        removals) so the user sees the bulk of the diff before being asked to resolve
700	        anything.

702	        The unreproducible carve-out is gone (D-18: that concern moved to
703	        `manual_installs_sync`); this override remains only for collateral.
704	        """
705	        collateral = [diff for diff in diffs if _is_collateral_diff(diff)]
706	        if not collateral:
707	            return super()._build_review_groups(diffs)
708	
709	        carved_ids = {diff.item_id for diff in collateral}
710	        rest = [diff for diff in diffs if diff.item_id not in carved_ids]
711	        groups = list(super()._build_review_groups(rest))
712	        groups.append(
713	            ReviewGroup(
714	                manager=self.manager_id,
715	                action=COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION,
716	                title=f"Resolve {self.manager_id} manual-collateral removals",
717	                entries=tuple(
718	                    ReviewEntry(item_id=diff.item_id, label=diff.label, action_label="resolve", detail=diff.detail)
719	                    for diff in collateral

904	    async def _collect_plan_time_collateral(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
905	        """Two BATCHED simulations — the whole install candidate set, the whole
906	        removal candidate set — not one per package: a per-package simulation over a
907	        150-package manual set would cost more than the sync itself (D-30 hangs its
908	        classification off these two results; no third simulation is added).
909	
910	        Each simulation's would-remove/would-downgrade collateral is split by
911	        `_classify_collateral` against the target's manual set: auto collateral produces
912	        nothing (apt's own business, D-30), manual collateral becomes a review item whose
913	        `item_id` (`apt:collateral:<name>`) is mapped back to the triggering candidate set
914	        in `self._collateral_trigger_ids`, so a `skip` decision can later be translated
915	        into `SKIP_ONCE` on the installs it gates.
916	        """

918	        # but is dpkg selection state, not an apt-get transaction, so it drives no
919	        # collateral simulation and its id is not a package id (#208).
920	        pkg = [d for d in diffs if d.item_class == ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE]
921	        install_names = [_package_name(d.item_id) for d in pkg if d.action == DiffAction.INSTALL]
922	        remove_names = [_package_name(d.item_id) for d in pkg if d.action == DiffAction.REMOVE]
923	        reviewed_names = frozenset(install_names) | frozenset(remove_names)
924	
925	        collateral: list[ItemDiff] = []
926	        if install_names:
927	            quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(name) for name in install_names)
928	            preview = await simulate_apt_transaction(
929	                self.target, f"install -y --no-install-recommends {quoted}", login_shell=False
930	            )
931	            trigger_ids = frozenset(f"{_APT_PACKAGE_ID_PREFIX}{name}" for name in install_names)
932	            collateral.extend(await self._classify_collateral(preview, reviewed_names, trigger_ids, verb="installing"))
933	        if remove_names:
934	            quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(name) for name in remove_names)
935	            preview = await simulate_apt_transaction(self.target, f"remove -y {quoted}", login_shell=False)
936	            trigger_ids = frozenset(f"{_APT_PACKAGE_ID_PREFIX}{name}" for name in remove_names)

940	    async def _classify_collateral(
941	        self,
942	        preview: AptTransactionPreview,
943	        reviewed_names: frozenset[str],
944	        trigger_ids: frozenset[str],
945	        *,
946	        verb: str,
947	    ) -> list[ItemDiff]:
948	        """Partition a simulation's would-remove/would-downgrade packages by provenance
949	        (D-30): a package in the target OR source manual set becomes a manual-collateral
950	        review item (decision 8); one in neither is auto-installed — apt's own dependency
951	        — and produces nothing, not even a report line the user cannot act on.
952	
953	        A downgrade is detected exactly as before: an `install_versions` entry with a
954	        non-`None` old version and `compare_deb_versions(target, new, old) < 0`. The
955	        triggering candidate set is recorded against each emitted item's id so `skip`
956	        can be translated to `SKIP_ONCE` on the installs it gates (`accept_review`).
957	        """
958	        protected = self._protected_manual_set()
959	        collateral: list[ItemDiff] = []
960	
961	        for pkg in preview.removals:
962	            if pkg in reviewed_names or pkg not in protected:
963	                continue
964	            collateral.append(
965	                self._collateral_item(pkg, f"would be removed by {verb} the selected packages", trigger_ids)
966	            )
967	
968	        for pkg, (old_version, new_version) in preview.install_versions.items():
969	            if pkg in reviewed_names or old_version is None or pkg not in protected:
970	                continue
971	            if await compare_deb_versions(self.target, new_version, old_version) < 0:
972	                effect = f"would be downgraded from {old_version} to {new_version} by {verb} the selected packages"
973	                collateral.append(self._collateral_item(pkg, effect, trigger_ids))
974	
975	        return collateral

979	        diff = _collateral_diff(name, effect)
980	        self._collateral_trigger_ids[diff.item_id] = trigger_ids

1002	    def _resolve_collateral(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> ReviewOutcome:
1003	        """Translate the manual-collateral group's decisions (D-30) into the guard's
1004	        approved set and the triggering installs' decisions.
1005	
1006	        For each collateral item (`apt:collateral:<pkg>`): an `APPLY` (install-anyway)
1007	        marks `<pkg>` approved, so `_converge_install`/`_converge_remove` let its removal
1008	        or downgrade through; a `SKIP_ONCE` (skip) is propagated to every install that
1009	        collateral gated (`self._collateral_trigger_ids`), so the install is cleanly left
1010	        unapproved rather than attempted and refused at the guard. Abort never reaches
1011	        here — it raised `SyncAbortedByUser` inside the review.
1012	
1013	        Returns the outcome with any triggering-install decisions overridden; leaves the
1014	        decisions map untouched when there is no collateral to resolve.
1015	        """
1016	        approved: set[str] = set()
1017	        overrides: dict[str, Decision] = {}
1018	        for diff in plan.diffs:
1019	            if not _is_collateral_diff(diff):
1020	                continue
1021	            decision = outcome.decisions.get(diff.item_id)
1022	            if decision == Decision.APPLY:
1023	                approved.add(diff.item_id.removeprefix(_COLLATERAL_ID_PREFIX))
1024	            elif decision == Decision.SKIP_ONCE:
1025	                for trigger_id in self._collateral_trigger_ids.get(diff.item_id, frozenset()):
1026	                    overrides[trigger_id] = Decision.SKIP_ONCE
1027	
1028	        self._approved_collateral = frozenset(approved)
1029	        if not overrides:
1030	            return outcome
1031	        return ReviewOutcome(
1032	            decisions={**outcome.decisions, **overrides},
1033	            was_interactive=outcome.was_interactive,
1034	            snippets=outcome.snippets,
1035	            unresolved=outcome.unresolved,
1036	        )

1040	        """Insert the synthetic metadata-refresh diff (Task 2) once the coordinator's
1041	        decisions are known, so it flows through the same per-item logging, dry-run
1042	        gate and failure collection as everything else (`apply()`'s existing loop)
1043	        instead of being a special case bolted onto the end.
1044	
1045	        Runs AFTER `plan()` (so decisions exist) and is exactly where D-24's review
1046	        already stopped being relevant for THIS item — the refresh is infrastructure
1047	        the user never ticks, not a repository or key they decided about. Positioned
1048	        immediately after the last non-package diff (repository group already sorted
1049	        key-before-pin/config-before-source by `plan()`) and before every package
1050	        diff, matching apt's own dependency order: metadata must be current before
1051	        anything installs from it.

1053	        Manual-collateral decisions (D-30) are resolved first: an install-anyway on a
1054	        collateral item marks its package approved so the apply-time guard lets the
1055	        removal through, while a skip is translated into `SKIP_ONCE` on the installs that
1056	        collateral gated, so a declined collateral cleanly leaves its triggering installs
1057	        unapproved rather than failing them at the guard.

1059	        outcome = self._resolve_collateral(plan, outcome)
1060	        approved_group = any(

1062	            and diff.item_id != _METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID
1063	            and outcome.decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY

1078	            outcome = ReviewOutcome(
