1242	    # -- Repository-group convergence (Task 2: D-11, D-12, D-13, D-27, T-02-34/35) -----
1243	    #
1244	    # The base `apply()` loop calls `converge()` once per approved diff, in `plan.diffs`
1245	    # order (already sorted key -> pin/config -> source -> metadata-refresh -> packages
1246	    # by `plan()`/`accept_review`). Rather than doing each repository-group item's work
1247	    # in ITS OWN `converge()` call — which would make the group's transactionality
1248	    # (backup everything before ANY write; roll back everything if the metadata refresh
1249	    # fails) impossible to express without the base loop knowing about groups — the
1250	    # FIRST repository-group (or metadata-refresh) diff `converge()` sees triggers
1251	    # `_ensure_repo_group_converged`, which does the WHOLE group's work right then:
1252	    # every subsequent group diff's `converge()` call is then a cache lookup against the
1253	    # per-item outcome that eager run recorded, including — critically — outcomes for
1254	    # diffs `converge()` has not been called for yet, and outcomes for diffs a rollback
1255	    # retroactively marks as failed even though their own write succeeded.
1256	
1257	    async def _converge_repo_group_item(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
1258	        await self._ensure_repo_group_converged()
1259	        assert self._repo_group_outcome is not None
1260	        succeeded, message = self._repo_group_outcome[diff.item_id]
1261	        if succeeded:
1262	            return CommandResult(exit_code=0, stdout=message, stderr="")
1263	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(message)

1268	        (`plan()`'s sort). Excludes the synthetic metadata-refresh marker itself, which
1269	        is tracked separately since it names no `/etc/apt` file to back up or write.
1270	        """
1271	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
1272	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
1273	        decisions = self._accepted_outcome.decisions
1274	        return [
1275	            diff
1276	            for diff in self._accepted_plan.diffs
1277	            if diff.item_class in _REPO_GROUP_CLASSES
1278	            and diff.item_id != _METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID
1279	            and diff.action in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.REMOVE, DiffAction.CHANGE)
1280	            and decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY

1283	    async def _ensure_repo_group_converged(self) -> None:
1284	        """Do the repository group's entire convergence exactly once per run: back up
1285	        every destination the group will touch, write/remove in the already-established
1286	        order, run ONE `apt-get update`, and roll back the whole group if it fails
1287	        (T-02-34) — never partially, since a failed metadata refresh with some files
1288	        written and others not would leave `/etc/apt` in a configuration nobody reviewed.
1289	
1290	        Idempotent: a no-op on every call after the first (`self._repo_group_outcome`
1291	        is `None` only until this method's first successful completion). Never called
1292	        under dry-run — the base `apply()` loop never calls `converge()` at all when
1293	        `self.context.dry_run` is set, so this method's own logic can assume real
1294	        commands are safe to issue.
1295	        """
1296	        if self._repo_group_outcome is not None:
1297	            return
1298	
1299	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
1300	        group_diffs = self._approved_repo_group_diffs()
1301	        marker_present = self._accepted_outcome.decisions.get(_METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID) == Decision.APPLY
1302	
1303	        if not group_diffs:
1304	            self._repo_group_outcome = (
1305	                {_METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID: (True, "no repository changes to refresh for")} if marker_present else {}
1306	            )
1307	            return
1308	
1309	        # Populated incrementally (not built up in a local dict and assigned at the
1310	        # end) so a later diff in THIS SAME group — a source item, converging after its
1311	        # key per the established order — can consult an earlier diff's real outcome
1312	        # via `_keyring_ready_on_target` while the group is still being written.
1313	        self._repo_group_outcome = {}
1314	
1315	        home = await self._target_home_dir()
1316	        staging_dir = f"{home}/.cache/pc-switcher/apt-staging"
1317	        backup_dir = f"{staging_dir}/backup-{uuid4().hex}"
1318	        await self.target.run_command(
1319	            f"mkdir -p {shlex.quote(staging_dir)}",
1320	            login_shell=False,
1321	            mutates="create the apt repository-group staging directory",
1322	        )
1323	
1324	        existed_before: dict[str, bool] = {}
1325	        try:
1326	            for diff in group_diffs:
1327	                dest = _repo_item_destination(diff)
1328	                existed_before[dest] = await self._backup_destination(dest, backup_dir)
1329	        except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
1330	            # A backup failure aborts the whole group before any write happens (T-02-34
1331	            # never partially applies), but `self._repo_group_outcome` must still end up
1332	            # populated for every group item (D-27) — otherwise the idempotency guard at
1333	            # the top of this method treats the group as "already handled" on the next
1334	            # `converge()` call, and `_converge_repo_group_item`'s
1335	            # `self._repo_group_outcome[diff.item_id]` raises a bare `KeyError` for every
1336	            # item after the first, escaping the per-item `ConvergeItemFailed` handler and
1337	            # crashing the whole job instead of failing one item.
1338	            self._record_group_failure(group_diffs, marker_present, f"repository group backup failed: {exc}")
1339	            return
1340	
1341	        for diff in group_diffs:
1342	            try:
1343	                await self._write_or_remove_repo_item(diff, staging_dir)
1344	                self._repo_group_outcome[diff.item_id] = (True, "converged")
1345	            except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
1346	                self._repo_group_outcome[diff.item_id] = (False, str(exc))
1347	
1348	        update_result = await self.target.run_command(
1349	            "sudo apt-get update",
1350	            login_shell=False,
1351	            mutates="refresh apt package lists against the newly written repository configuration",
1352	        )
1353	        if update_result.success:
1354	            # This IS the run's single metadata refresh (decision 1): flag it so the
1355	            # install path's `_ensure_metadata_refreshed` is a no-op and never issues a
1356	            # second `apt-get update`.
1357	            self._metadata_refreshed = True
1358	            await self.target.run_command(
1359	                f"rm -rf {shlex.quote(backup_dir)}",
1360	                login_shell=False,
1361	                mutates="discard the repository-group backup after a successful refresh",
1362	            )
1363	            if marker_present:
1364	                self._repo_group_outcome[_METADATA_REFRESH_ITEM_ID] = (True, "apt-get update succeeded")
1365	            return
1366	
1367	        # Rollback (T-02-34): restore every file that existed before, delete every file
1368	        # the group created, discard the backup directory, then re-probe apt so the
1369	        # failure summary can tell the user whether the target recovered rather than
1370	        # leaving them to guess.
1371	        recovery = await self._rollback_repo_group(existed_before, backup_dir)
1372	        self._log(
1373	            Host.TARGET,
1374	            LogLevel.ERROR,
1375	            f"apt-get update failed after repository group writes; rolled back ({recovery}): "
1376	            f"{update_result.stderr.strip()}",
1377	            stderr=update_result.stderr,
1378	        )
1379	
1380	        # Every group item is recorded as a failure (D-27) — even ones whose own write
1381	        # just succeeded above — because the rollback undid it: what actually landed on
1382	        # the target is the pre-run state, not what this run intended.
1383	        self._record_group_failure(
1384	            group_diffs,
1385	            marker_present,
1386	            f"repository group rolled back after apt-get update failure ({recovery}): {update_result.stderr.strip()}",
1387	        )

1389	    async def _rollback_repo_group(self, existed_before: dict[str, bool], backup_dir: str) -> str:
1390	        """Undo the repository group's writes and re-probe apt; return a short phrase
1391	        describing how the target ended up, for the caller's failure summary (T-02-34).
1392	
1393	        Restores every file that existed before the group ran, deletes every file the
1394	        group created, discards the backup, then runs `apt-get update` so the summary can
1395	        state whether the target recovered rather than leaving the user to guess.
1396	
1397	        One command per file, each result inspected. A single `;`-joined command would
1398	        present the `--confirm-each-command` gate one all-or-nothing prompt, but it
1399	        collapses N exit codes into one and makes "which file failed to restore"
1400	        unanswerable — and a failing rollback step is exactly when the user needs that
1401	        file named. Every step is attempted regardless of earlier failures, so one
1402	        unwritable destination cannot strand the remaining files in their post-run state.
1403	        """
1404	        rollback_failures: list[str] = []
1405	        for dest, existed in existed_before.items():
1406	            if existed:
1407	                backup_path = _backup_path_for(backup_dir, dest)
1408	                action = f"restore {dest} from {backup_path}"
1409	                result = await self.target.run_command(
1410	                    f"sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 {shlex.quote(backup_path)} {shlex.quote(dest)}",
1411	                    login_shell=False,
1412	                    mutates=f"ROLLBACK: restore {dest} from backup",
1413	                )
1414	            else:
1415	                action = f"delete {dest}, which this run created"
1416	                result = await self.target.run_command(
1417	                    f"sudo rm -f {shlex.quote(dest)}",
1418	                    login_shell=False,
1419	                    mutates=f"ROLLBACK: delete {dest}, which this run created",
1420	                )
1421	            if not result.success:
1422	                rollback_failures.append(f"could not {action}: {result.stderr.strip()}")
1423	                self._log(
1424	                    Host.TARGET,
1425	                    LogLevel.WARNING,
1426	                    f"Rollback step failed — could not {action}: {result.stderr.strip()}",
1427	                    stderr=result.stderr,
1428	                )
1429	
1430	        if rollback_failures:
1431	            # The backup directory is deliberately NOT discarded: a failed restore means it
1432	            # holds the only remaining copy of that file's pre-run content, so deleting it
1433	            # would destroy exactly what manual recovery depends on. Name the path — the
1434	            # user has to finish this by hand.
1435	            self._log(
1436	                Host.TARGET,
1437	                LogLevel.WARNING,
1438	                f"Repository-group rollback incomplete; the backup is kept at {backup_dir} on the target "
1439	                f"so the affected file(s) can be restored by hand: {'; '.join(rollback_failures)}",
1440	            )
1441	        else:
1442	            await self.target.run_command(
1443	                f"rm -rf {shlex.quote(backup_dir)}",
1444	                login_shell=False,
1445	                mutates="ROLLBACK: discard the repository-group backup directory",
1446	            )
1447	
1448	        reprobe = await self.target.run_command(
1449	            "sudo apt-get update",
1450	            login_shell=False,
1451	            mutates="ROLLBACK: re-probe apt against the restored repository configuration",
1452	        )
1453	        if reprobe.success:
1454	            # After rollback `/etc/apt` is the pre-run configuration and this reprobe refreshed
1455	            # metadata for it; package installs that still run against that config (D-27 —
1456	            # a repo-group rollback does not cancel package items) then need no further
1457	            # `apt-get update`. If the reprobe itself failed, the flag stays unset and the
1458	            # install path's own refresh attempt will surface the still-broken apt.
1459	            self._metadata_refreshed = True
1460	
1461	        if rollback_failures:
1462	            # Takes precedence over the reprobe's verdict: an incomplete rollback leaves
1463	            # /etc/apt as neither the pre-run nor the post-run configuration, which a green
1464	            # `apt-get update` would otherwise mask.
1465	            return (
1466	                f"ROLLBACK INCOMPLETE, {len(rollback_failures)} file(s) left unrestored "
1467	                f"(backup kept at {backup_dir}): {'; '.join(rollback_failures)}"
1468	            )
1469	        return "target apt recovered after rollback" if reprobe.success else "target apt still broken after rollback"

1473	        as failed with `message`. Shared by the backup-failure short-circuit and the

1510	    async def _write_or_remove_repo_item(self, diff: ItemDiff, staging_dir: str) -> None:
1511	        """Converge one repository-group diff: `sudo rm -f` for a REMOVE, or
1512	        stage-then-promote for an INSTALL/CHANGE (T-02-35). `RemoteExecutor.send_file`
1513	        is plain SFTP as the ordinary SSH user with no sudo path (`executor.py` around
1514	        line 362) and cannot write into `/etc/apt` directly — bytes land under the
1515	        target user's own `~/.cache` staging directory first, then `sudo install`
1516	        promotes them with the right ownership/mode in one atomic step (no window where
1517	        the file exists under `/etc/apt` owned by the wrong user, unlike a `mv` +
1518	        separate `chown`/`chmod`). The staging copy is removed in a `finally` so a
1519	        failed promotion never leaves transferred key material sitting in the cache.
1520	        """
1521	        dest = _repo_item_destination(diff)
1522	
1523	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
1524	            result = await self.target.run_command(
1525	                f"sudo rm -f {shlex.quote(dest)}",
1526	                login_shell=False,
1527	                mutates=f"delete repository file {dest}",
1528	            )
1529	            if not result.success:
1530	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"failed to remove {dest}: {result.stderr.strip()}")
1531	            return
1532	
1533	        if diff.item_class == ItemClass.APT_SOURCE:
1534	            await self._require_keyrings_ready(diff)
1535	
1536	        # `sources.list.d`, `preferences.d`, `apt.conf.d` and `trusted.gpg.d` ship with
1537	        # the `apt` package, but `/etc/apt/keyrings` is a third-party convention that a
1538	        # fresh Ubuntu 24.04 target does not have — `install` (unlike `install -D`)
1539	        # never creates DEST's missing parent directories, so a per-repo key promotion
1540	        # to a fresh machine would otherwise fail every time. `mkdir -p -m` only chmods
1541	        # directories it actually creates (unlike `install -d`, which would also chmod
1542	        # the four directories that already exist), so this is a no-op everywhere except
1543	        # the one directory this project actually needs to create.
1544	        dest_dir = str(Path(dest).parent)
1545	        mkdir_result = await self.target.run_command(
1546	            f"sudo mkdir -p -m 0755 {shlex.quote(dest_dir)}",
1547	            login_shell=False,
1548	            mutates=f"create directory {dest_dir} for {dest}",
1549	        )

1552	                f"failed to prepare directory {dest_dir} for {dest}: {mkdir_result.stderr.strip()}"
1553	            )

1555	        local_path = Path(dest)

1563	                f"sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 {shlex.quote(staged_dest)} {shlex.quote(dest)}",
1564	                login_shell=False,

1573	                mutates=f"remove the staging copy of {dest}",
1574	            )

1576	    async def _require_keyrings_ready(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> None:
1577	        """Refuse to write a source file whose keyring reference is neither already
1578	        matching on the target nor among this run's successfully converged key items
1579	        (Task 2, D-12) — a repository written without its key is a repository apt
1580	        refuses on every subsequent operation, which makes writing it anyway strictly
1581	        worse than leaving the target alone.
1582	
1583	        Re-reads and re-parses the source file's own content rather than threading the
1584	        already-parsed `AptSourceItem.keyring_refs` through the plan/diff pipeline: the
1585	        plan only carries `ItemDiff`s (module docstring — one shared shape for every
1586	        item class), so re-deriving from the source's own bytes at converge time is the
1587	        cost of keeping that shape uniform, and the file is small enough that a second
1588	        `cat` is negligible next to the write it gates.
1589	        """
1590	        filename = diff.item_id.removeprefix("apt:source:")
1591	        source_path = f"{_APT_SOURCES_DIR}/{filename}"
1592	        content = await _read_file_content(self.source.run_command, source_path)
1593	        _fmt, refs = _parse_source_file(filename, content)
1594	
1595	        for ref in refs:
1596	            ref_filename = Path(ref).name
1597	            if self._keyring_ready_on_target(ref_filename):
1598	                continue
1599	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
1600	                f"source {filename} references keyring {ref_filename!r}, which is neither already "
1601	                "present on the target nor among this run's successfully converged key items "
1602	                "(D-12/T-02-16); skipping this repository write"
1603	            )

1605	    def _keyring_ready_on_target(self, ref_filename: str) -> bool:
1606	        """A keyring reference is ready for a source file to depend on if it already
1607	        matches byte-for-byte on the target (no diff was even needed, per the digest
1608	        maps `_plan_repo_diffs` captured) or if this run already successfully converged
1609	        it (checked against `_repo_group_outcome`, which — because keys sort before
1610	        sources — already holds every key diff's real outcome by the time a source
1611	        diff's own write is attempted).
1612	        """
1613	        source_digest = self._source_key_digests_by_filename.get(ref_filename)
1614	        target_digest = self._target_key_digests_by_filename.get(ref_filename)
1615	        if source_digest is not None and source_digest == target_digest:
1616	            return True
1617	        if self._repo_group_outcome is not None:
1618	            for scope in ("per-repo", "global-trust"):
1619	                outcome = self._repo_group_outcome.get(f"apt:key:{scope}:{ref_filename}")
1620	                if outcome is not None and outcome[0]:
1621	                    return True
1622	        return False

1	"""`snap_sync`: snap name/channel/revision convergence through snapd's own verbs
2	(D-06, D-14, D-29, ADR-020).
3	
4	WARNING — `snap refresh --hold` with NO snap name is a MUTATING command: called that
5	way it silently sets an INDEFINITE GLOBAL hold on auto-refresh for every snap on the
6	machine (RESEARCH Pitfall 1 — discovered live against a real machine during Phase 2
7	research, and only undone with a manual `snap refresh --unhold`). This module never
8	calls it. Hold state is inspected only through the read-only `snap get system
9	refresh.hold` (`validate()`, informational only, never acted on). Convergence uses
10	only `snap install --revision=<N>` and `snap refresh --revision=<N>`, which land the
11	target on the source's exact revision without touching the standing auto-refresh
12	policy at all — the mechanism D-06 requires: both machines converge on the same
13	revision, neither stops updating.
14	
15	The snapd store stays authoritative for its own state (D-01): this job never touches
16	`/var/lib/snapd` directly, only shells out to `snap` itself, the same shape
17	`apt_sync` uses for `apt`/`dpkg`.
18	
19	`SnapSyncJob` subclasses `PackageSyncJob` but overrides `plan()` rather than
20	inheriting the base implementation: `PackageSyncJob.diff_items`/`_diff_apt_packages`
21	is apt-package-shaped (a version difference is `REPORT_ONLY` per D-04, and it has no
22	notion of a tracking channel), while D-06 wants a snap's revision AND channel
23	differences to actively converge (`CHANGE`). `plan()` here reuses the same shared
24	building blocks apt_sync's own diff-taxonomy plan relies on — `DecisionFile`/
25	`filter_inert` (D-08's machine-local skip-always filtering) and
26	`PackageSyncJob._build_review_groups` (D-24's action-grouped review) — so the only
27	genuinely snap-specific code is capture, diff and converge. `accept_review()`,
28	`apply()` and `execute()` are inherited unchanged; this job implements no review of
29	its own — the coordinator (plan 02-03) reviews every enabled manager at once.
30	
31	Revision AND channel differences share one `DiffAction.CHANGE` diff per snap, tagged
32	`ItemClass.SNAP` in both cases (never `ItemClass.SNAP_CHANNEL`) even though a
33	same-revision retrack is conceptually "just" a channel change: `PackageSyncJob.
34	_build_review_groups` derives one action_label verb per REVIEW GROUP from its first
35	entry's `item_class` (its own docstring flags this as unhandled for "a manager mixing
36	item classes under one action"), so tagging some CHANGE diffs `SNAP` and others
37	`SNAP_CHANNEL` would risk one of the two kinds getting the other's verb whenever both
38	occur in the same run. Using one item_class for every CHANGE diff avoids that
39	mislabeling entirely; the diff's `detail` text still names both revisions or both
40	channels, satisfying D-07's "review names the concrete action" without depending on a
41	shared-core behavior this plan does not own.
42	"""

97	def _parse_snap_list(output: str) -> list[SnapItem]:
98	    """Parse `snap list --all` by HEADER column names, never fixed offsets or assumed
99	    order (RESEARCH Open Question 2): a future snapd column reorder must yield correct
100	    values, never a silently wrong revision driving a wrong `--revision` install.
101	
102	    Skips a disabled older-revision line (`Notes` names `disabled`) for a snap that
103	    also has an active line — only the active revision becomes the item. Output shaped
104	    like "No snaps are installed yet." (no recognizable header) degrades to an empty
105	    list rather than raising: a snap-free machine is a valid, if rare, state.
106	    """
107	    lines = [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
108	    if not lines:
109	        return []
110	
111	    header = lines[0].split()
112	    try:
113	        name_idx = header.index("Name")
114	        rev_idx = header.index("Rev")
115	        tracking_idx = header.index("Tracking")
116	        notes_idx = header.index("Notes")
117	    except ValueError:
118	        return []
119	
120	    max_idx = max(name_idx, rev_idx, tracking_idx, notes_idx)
121	    items: list[SnapItem] = []
122	    for line in lines[1:]:
123	        fields = line.split()
124	        if len(fields) <= max_idx:
125	            continue
126	        notes = fields[notes_idx].split(",")
127	        if "disabled" in notes:
128	            continue
129	        # `held` in the Notes column is a PER-SNAP refresh hold (#208, D9) — snapstate
130	        # attached to this one snap. It is SEPARATE state from the system-wide
131	        # `refresh.hold` the orchestrator sets across the sync window via `snap set
132	        # system refresh.hold` (different snapd namespaces), so capturing here, inside
133	        # the sync window, does not mask a per-snap hold: the system hold never writes
134	        # `held` into an individual snap's Notes. If a VM integration test ever shows a
135	        # system hold flipping this token, capture would have to move BEFORE the
136	        # sync-window hold is applied. Fail-safe even then: a system hold flips both
137	        # hosts symmetrically -> both-held -> no spurious diff.
138	        held = "held" in notes
139	        items.append(
140	            SnapItem(name=fields[name_idx], channel=fields[tracking_idx], revision=fields[rev_idx], held=held)
141	        )
142	    return items

189	    `AptHoldItem`): `in_source` (source-held, target-not) -> INSTALL (hold on target);
190	    otherwise (target-held, source-not) -> REMOVE (unhold on target). The identity
191	    (`snap:hold:<name>`) is DISTINCT from the snap item's (`snap:<name>`) so a snap and
192	    its hold are two separate review items.
193	    """
194	    return ItemDiff(
195	        item_class=ItemClass.SNAP_HOLD,
196	        diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET if in_source else DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
197	        action=DiffAction.INSTALL if in_source else DiffAction.REMOVE,

204	def _diff_snap_holds(source_items: Sequence[SnapItem], target_items: Sequence[SnapItem]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
205	    """Per-snap hold membership diffs (#208, D2), emitted AFTER the presence diffs so
206	    install-before-hold ordering holds (`apply()` preserves diff order): source-held &
207	    not target-held -> INSTALL (hold); target-held & not source-held -> REMOVE (unhold);
208	    both-held or neither -> no diff.
209	
210	    Only snaps present on the SOURCE are considered — source is authoritative for hold
211	    intent (a hold on a snap the source no longer has is not the user's current intent).
212	    `sorted` for a stable, deterministic review order.
213	    """
214	    source_by_name = {item.name: item for item in source_items}
215	    target_held = {item.name for item in target_items if item.held}
216	
217	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
218	    for name in sorted(source_by_name):
219	        in_source = source_by_name[name].held
220	        in_target = name in target_held
221	        if in_source == in_target:
222	            continue
223	        diffs.append(_hold_diff(name, in_source=in_source))
224	    return diffs

227	def _diff_snap_items(source_items: Sequence[SnapItem], target_items: Sequence[SnapItem]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
228	    """One diff per snap name present on either side, source-then-target order — same
229	    shape as `PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_packages`, but with D-06's own convergence rule.
230	    Per-snap hold membership diffs follow the presence diffs (D8: install-before-hold).
231	    """
232	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
233	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
234	
235	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
236	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
237	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
238	
239	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
240	    for item_id in seen:
241	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
242	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
243	
244	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
245	            diffs.append(_install_diff(source_item))
246	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
247	            diffs.append(_remove_diff(target_item))
248	        elif (
249	            source_item is not None
250	            and target_item is not None
251	            and (source_item.revision != target_item.revision or source_item.channel != target_item.channel)
252	        ):
253	            diffs.append(_change_diff(item_id, source_item, target_item))
254	        # else: present on both, identical revision and channel -> no diff.
255	
256	    # Hold diffs AFTER presence diffs (D8) so a hold on a same-run install lands once the
257	    # snap is present.
258	    diffs.extend(_diff_snap_holds(source_items, target_items))
259	
260	    return diffs

263	def _current_revision_name(app_dir: Path) -> str | None:
264	    """The revision directory name `~/<app>/current` resolves to, or None when the
265	    symlink is missing or dangling.
266	
267	    snapd maintains `current` as a symlink to the active revision's directory. Resolving
268	    it (readlink, followed to the real dir) yields that revision's directory name so the
269	    caller can keep the matching data dir in the mirror (decision 3). A missing or dangling
270	    `current` — the active revision is then indeterminate — returns None, and the caller
271	    falls back to excluding every revision dir for that app (the safe default).
272	    """
273	    current = app_dir / "current"
274	    try:
275	        resolved = current.resolve(strict=True)
276	    except OSError:
277	        return None
278	    if not resolved.is_dir():
279	        return None
280	    return resolved.name

283	def snap_sync_exclude_paths() -> list[Path]:
284	    """Absolute `~/snap/<app>/<revision>` data directories folder_sync must NOT mirror,
285	    resolved against `Path.home()` at call time exactly like `vscode_state_exclude_paths()`
286	    — unlike VS Code's fixed relpath list, the revision set is dynamic, so it is enumerated
287	    from the filesystem rather than hardcoded.
288	
289	    Per app this excludes every revision dir EXCEPT the one the app's `current` symlink
290	    resolves to (decision 3, issue #118): snap_sync converges the target onto the source's
291	    revision before folder_sync runs (D-17 order), so by folder_sync time both machines'
292	    `current` points at the same revision, and mirroring THAT revision's data dir carries
293	    the active revision's per-user app data across. The retained older revision dirs stay
294	    excluded so folder_sync never plants data dirs for revisions the target's snapd never
295	    installed.
296	
297	    `~/snap/<app>/common` (revision-independent user data folder_sync must keep mirroring)
298	    and `~/snap/<app>/current` (the symlink itself) are always kept — the whole reason this
299	    export is not simply `~/snap`. When `current` is missing or dangling the active revision
300	    cannot be determined, so ALL of that app's revision dirs are excluded (safe default).
301	    """
302	    snap_root = Path.home() / "snap"
303	    if not snap_root.is_dir():
304	        return []
305	
306	    paths: list[Path] = []
307	    for app_dir in sorted(snap_root.iterdir()):
308	        if not app_dir.is_dir():
309	            continue
310	        current_revision = _current_revision_name(app_dir)
311	        for entry in sorted(app_dir.iterdir()):
312	            if entry.name in _NON_REVISION_DIR_NAMES or not entry.is_dir():
313	                continue
314	            if current_revision is not None and entry.name == current_revision:
315	                continue  # active-revision data dir travels with folder_sync (decision 3)
316	            paths.append(entry)
317	    return paths

320	class SnapSyncJob(PackageSyncJob):
321	    """Converge snap name/channel/revision after the coordinator's batched review.
322	
323	    Overrides `plan()` with a snap-specific capture -> diff -> review-group pipeline
324	    (module docstring explains why the inherited apt-package-shaped one cannot be
325	    reused); `accept_review()`, `apply()` and `execute()` are inherited unchanged.
326	    """
327	
328	    name: ClassVar[str] = "snap_sync"
329	    manager_id: ClassVar[str] = "snap"
330	
331	    # No configurable properties: mirrors AptSyncJob's empty schema — only the enable
332	    # flag in sync_jobs is needed for this slice.
333	    CONFIG_SCHEMA: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {
334	        "type": "object",
335	        "properties": {},
336	        "additionalProperties": False,
337	    }
338	
339	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
340	        super().__init__(context)
341	        # Populated by plan()'s own capture/query step (post filter_inert) and
342	        # consulted by converge(): the base pipeline only ever hands converge() an
343	        # ItemDiff, whose item_id ("snap:<name>") carries no revision/channel data of
344	        # its own — unlike an apt package name, `snap install --revision=N` needs the
345	        # literal N, which has to come from somewhere other than the diff itself.
346	        self._source_items_by_id: dict[str, SnapItem] = {}
347	        self._target_items_by_id: dict[str, SnapItem] = {}
348	
349	    @override
350	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[SnapItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
351	        """`snap list --all` on the source (D-06).
352	
353	        This job overrides `plan()` and never routes through `PackageSyncJob.
354	        diff_items`'s apt-package-shaped dispatch (module docstring), so widening this
355	        hook's item type here is safe: no code holding a `PackageSyncJob`-typed
356	        reference ever calls it expecting an `AptPackageItem` back.
357	        """
358	        result = await self.source.run_command("snap list --all")
359	        return _parse_snap_list(result.stdout)
360	
361	    @override
362	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[SnapItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
363	        """The target's own `snap list --all` (same reasoning as `capture_source_items`)."""
364	        result = await self.target.run_command("snap list --all", login_shell=False)
365	        return _parse_snap_list(result.stdout)
366	
367	    @override
368	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
369	        """Load decision files -> capture -> query -> diff -> build review groups.
370	
371	        Read-only: only `snap list --all` (both machines) and a decision-file `cat`
372	        run here — no `snap install`/`refresh`/`switch`/`remove` before this returns.
373	        Caches the filtered source/target items by id for `converge()` (see
374	        `__init__`), since `ItemDiff.item_id` alone carries no revision/channel data.
375	        """
376	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
377	        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
378	
379	        source_items = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
380	        target_items = await filter_inert(await self.query_target_items(), target_decisions)
381	
382	        self._source_items_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
383	        self._target_items_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
384	
385	        diffs = tuple(_diff_snap_items(source_items, target_items))
386	        groups = self._build_review_groups(diffs)
387	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=diffs, groups=groups)
388	
389	    @override
390	    async def converge(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
391	        """Install/refresh at the source's explicit revision, switch channel only when
392	        it differs, or remove (never purge) — the only D-06-safe verbs (module
393	        docstring). One snap per invocation (D-27) so a single bad snap cannot fail the
394	        whole batch.
395	
396	        Hold membership items (`snap:hold:<name>`) are routed FIRST, by item_id prefix
397	        (#208, D4), so a `snap:hold:` INSTALL runs `snap refresh --hold=forever` rather
398	        than a snap install, and a `snap:hold:` REMOVE (unhold) is never misread as a
399	        snap removal. This test MUST precede the action-based dispatch below, because
400	        `snap:hold:` also matches the plain `snap:` prefix.
401	        """
402	        if diff.item_id.startswith(_SNAP_HOLD_ID_PREFIX):
403	            return await self._converge_hold(diff)
404	
405	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
406	            return await self._converge_remove(diff)
407	
408	        source_item = self._source_items_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
409	        if source_item is None:
410	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
411	                f"no captured source snap for {diff.label} (item_id={diff.item_id!r}); "
412	                "was plan() run before converge()?"
413	            )
414	
415	        if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL:
416	            return await self._converge_install(source_item)
417	        if diff.action == DiffAction.CHANGE:
418	            target_item = self._target_items_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
419	            return await self._converge_change(source_item, target_item)
420	
421	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"SnapSyncJob.converge: unsupported action {diff.action.value!r} for {diff.label}")
422	
423	    async def _converge_install(self, source_item: SnapItem) -> CommandResult:
424	        """`snap install --revision=<N>` lands the exact revision without ever
425	        touching a hold (D-06); the channel switch always follows so the target
426	        tracks the same channel as the source. There is no cheap way to learn
427	        "snapd's default channel for a not-yet-installed snap" from `snap list --all`
428	        alone (only installed snaps appear in it), and re-running `switch` to a
429	        channel the install already landed on is a harmless no-op, so always
430	        switching is simpler and no less correct than conditioning on that unknown.
431	        """
432	        name = shlex.quote(source_item.name)
433	        revision = shlex.quote(source_item.revision)
434	        install_result = await self.target.run_command(
435	            f"sudo snap install --revision={revision} {name}",
436	            login_shell=False,
437	            mutates=f"install snap {source_item.name} at revision {source_item.revision}",
438	        )
439	        if not install_result.success:
440	            return install_result
441	        return await self._switch_channel(source_item)
442	
443	    async def _converge_change(self, source_item: SnapItem, target_item: SnapItem | None) -> CommandResult:
444	        """`snap refresh --revision=<N>` when the revision differs, plus the channel
445	        switch when the channel also differs (or is the only thing that differs) —
446	        `converge()` only reaches here for a diff `_diff_snap_items` built because at
447	        least one of the two was true.
448	        """
449	        revision_differs = target_item is None or source_item.revision != target_item.revision
450	        channel_differs = target_item is None or source_item.channel != target_item.channel
451	
452	        result: CommandResult | None = None
453	        if revision_differs:
454	            name = shlex.quote(source_item.name)
455	            revision = shlex.quote(source_item.revision)
456	            result = await self.target.run_command(
457	                f"sudo snap refresh --revision={revision} {name}",
458	                login_shell=False,
459	                mutates=f"move snap {source_item.name} to revision {source_item.revision}",
460	            )
461	            if not result.success:
462	                return result
463	
464	        if channel_differs:
465	            result = await self._switch_channel(source_item)
466	
467	        assert result is not None, "converge() only calls this for a diff where something differed at plan time"
468	        return result
469	
470	    async def _switch_channel(self, source_item: SnapItem) -> CommandResult:
471	        name = shlex.quote(source_item.name)
472	        channel = shlex.quote(source_item.channel)
473	        return await self.target.run_command(
474	            f"sudo snap switch --channel={channel} {name}",
475	            login_shell=False,
476	            mutates=f"track channel {source_item.channel} for snap {source_item.name}",
477	        )
478	
479	    async def _converge_remove(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
480	        """`snap remove`, never `--purge`: purge discards snapd's own pre-removal
481	        snapshot, which is the user's only recovery path if the removal was a mistake.
482	        """
483	        name = shlex.quote(_snap_name(diff.item_id))
484	        return await self.target.run_command(
485	            f"sudo snap remove {name}",
486	            login_shell=False,
487	            mutates=f"remove snap {_snap_name(diff.item_id)}",
488	        )
489	
490	    async def _converge_hold(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
491	        """Converge one `snap:hold:<name>` membership item (#208, D4/D6): INSTALL ->
492	        `snap refresh --hold=forever <name>` (per-snap hold on the target), REMOVE ->
493	        `snap refresh --unhold <name>`.
494	
495	        CRITICAL (module docstring, RESEARCH Pitfall 1): the snap name is ALWAYS
496	        interpolated, so this never degenerates into a bare `snap refresh --hold` — the
497	        form that silently sets an INDEFINITE GLOBAL hold on every snap. The name comes
498	        from the item_id's `snap:hold:` suffix, which `_diff_snap_holds` only ever built
499	        from a concrete source/target snap name, so it is never empty.
500	
501	        Selection state only, no gating (D6): a hold on a snap the user skipped
502	        installing this run hits an absent snap and fails — that is a normal per-item
503	        failure (D-27, the exit code alone decides pass/fail), not a gated abort.
504	        """
505	        raw_name = diff.item_id.removeprefix(_SNAP_HOLD_ID_PREFIX)
506	        name = shlex.quote(raw_name)
507	        flag = "--hold=forever" if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL else "--unhold"
508	        verb = "hold" if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL else "unhold"
509	        return await self.target.run_command(
510	            f"sudo snap refresh {flag} {name}",
511	            login_shell=False,
512	            mutates=f"{verb} snap {raw_name}",
513	        )
514	
515	    @override
516	    async def validate(self) -> list[ValidationError]:
517	        """`snap version` on both ends, passwordless `sudo -n true` on BOTH ends, and a
518	        read-only informational hold check on both ends (never acted on — module docstring).
519	        Sequential checks appending to `errors`, matching `AptSyncJob.validate()`'s shape.
520	
521	        Passwordless sudo is now required on the SOURCE too, not just the target: the
522	        orchestrator pauses snapd auto-refresh across the sync window by writing
523	        `refresh.hold` via `sudo snap set system` on both hosts (decision 4), so the source
524	        needs the same `sudo -n` grant for `/usr/bin/snap` that the target already needed
525	        for install/refresh/remove.
526	        """
527	        errors: list[ValidationError] = []
528	
529	        source_check = await self.source.run_command("snap version")
530	        if not source_check.success:
531	            errors.append(self._validation_error(Host.SOURCE, "snap is not available on source"))
532	
533	        target_check = await self.target.run_command("snap version", login_shell=False)
534	        if not target_check.success:
535	            errors.append(self._validation_error(Host.TARGET, "snap is not available on target"))
536	
537	        source_sudo_check = await self.source.run_command("sudo -n true")
538	        if not source_sudo_check.success:
539	            errors.append(
540	                self._validation_error(
541	                    Host.SOURCE,
542	                    "passwordless sudo is not available on source "
543	                    "(required to pause snapd auto-refresh for the sync window).\n"
544	                    + passwordless_sudo_hint(_TARGET_SUDO_COMMANDS),
545	                )
546	            )
547	
548	        sudo_check = await self.target.run_command("sudo -n true", login_shell=False)
549	        if not sudo_check.success:
550	            errors.append(
551	                self._validation_error(
552	                    Host.TARGET,
553	                    "passwordless sudo is not available on target "
554	                    "(required for snap install/refresh/remove).\n"
555	                    + passwordless_sudo_hint(_TARGET_SUDO_COMMANDS, user=self.context.target_username),
556	                )
557	            )
558	
559	        # Read-only informational context (RESEARCH Pitfall 1): NEVER `snap refresh
560	        # --hold` with no arguments to check this — that form mutates. A pre-existing
561	        # hold is not itself an error here; it only explains why a revision might not
562	        # converge, so it is logged, never appended to `errors`.
563	        source_hold = await self.source.run_command("snap get system refresh.hold")
564	        self._log(Host.SOURCE, LogLevel.FULL, f"source snap refresh.hold: {source_hold.stdout.strip() or '(none)'}")
565	        target_hold = await self.target.run_command("snap get system refresh.hold", login_shell=False)
566	        self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"target snap refresh.hold: {target_hold.stdout.strip() or '(none)'}")
567	
568	        return errors

1	"""`flatpak_sync`: flatpak ref/remote convergence with scope as identity (D-06, D-14,
2	D-29, ADR-020).
3	
4	Scope (user vs. system) is part of a flatpak item's identity, not just a field on it:
5	this project's own reference machine has several runtimes installed in BOTH scopes
6	under the same application id, and `FlatpakItem.item_id`/`FlatpakRemoteItem.item_id`
7	already fold scope into the identity string (`packages/items.py`). That is what makes
8	"same application, different scope" fall out of the generic source-vs-target diff as
9	two independent items with no special-casing in this module — a ref present as
10	`user` on the source and `system` on the target produces one install diff and one
11	removal diff, never a single in-place change, because they are simply two different
12	`item_id`s. Normalising that scope split across a machine's own two installations is
13	explicitly out of scope (deferred, CONTEXT.md): it is a change to the machines, not a
14	sync feature, and this job reports the split exactly as found.
15	
16	`flatpak install` refuses outright when the remote it names is not yet configured in
17	the scope being installed into (D-14), so remotes are captured and diffed as their
18	own item class (`FLATPAK_REMOTE`) and this job's own ordering stage (mirroring
19	`apt_sync`'s key-before-source sort) places every remote diff ahead of every ref diff
20	before the plan's `diffs` tuple ever reaches `apply()`'s per-diff loop. Before
21	converging a ref, its origin remote is checked against what already exists on the
22	target in that scope OR what this SAME run has already successfully added — a ref
23	whose remote is missing from both is skipped with a per-item failure naming the
24	remote, rather than issuing an install flatpak will reject (T-02-24).
25	
26	The flatpak OSTree store stays authoritative for its own state (D-01): this job never
27	touches `/var/lib/flatpak` or `~/.local/share/flatpak` directly, only shells out to
28	`flatpak` itself. `flatpak_sync_exclude_paths()` exports `~/.local/share/flatpak` so
29	`folder_sync` stops mirroring the store this job owns (D-29, ADR-018) — but NOT
30	`~/.var/app`, which is per-application USER DATA that stays folder_sync's territory;
31	D-17's job-before-folder_sync ordering exists precisely so `flatpak install` creates
32	the store first and folder_sync's data lands on top of it, never the reverse.
33	
34	`FlatpakSyncJob` subclasses `PackageSyncJob` but overrides `plan()` rather than
35	inheriting the base implementation, for the same reason `SnapSyncJob` does (see that
36	module's docstring and 02-08's own deviation note): `PackageSyncJob.diff_items`/
37	`_diff_apt_packages` is apt-package-shaped — one item class, `MISSING_ON_TARGET`/
38	`EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`VERSION_MISMATCH` only, no notion of a second item class that must
39	converge ahead of the first. This job diffs and converges THREE item classes
40	(`FLATPAK_REMOTE`, `FLATPAK_REF`, `FLATPAK_MASK`) with an ordering dependency between
41	them (remotes -> refs -> masks, D-08/D-14), which the shared dispatch has no way to
42	express. `plan()` here reuses every manager-agnostic
43	building block the shared core provides — `DecisionFile`/`filter_inert` (D-08's
44	machine-local skip-always filtering) and `PackageSyncJob._build_review_groups`
45	(D-24's action-grouped review) — so only capture, diff and converge are genuinely
46	flatpak-specific. `accept_review()`, `apply()` and `execute()` are inherited
47	unchanged; this job implements no review of its own — the coordinator (plan 02-03)
48	reviews every enabled manager at once, and this module never calls that reviewing
49	function directly.
50	
51	Flatpak ref VERSIONS are captured for reporting only (D-04, like apt package
52	versions): a version difference on a ref present in the same scope on both machines
53	is a `REPORT_ONLY` diff, never something this job installs or removes to force.
54	"""

112	def _lines(output: str) -> list[str]:
113	    """Non-blank lines, exactly as every tab-separated `flatpak` list command in this
114	    module produces them — no per-field stripping, since a real flatpak app id, remote
115	    name or URL never carries leading/trailing whitespace of its own.
116	    """
117	    return [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]

125	    """`sudo ` for a system-scope converge command, empty for user-scope (T-02-23,
126	    ASVS V4): `--system` writes into `/var/lib/flatpak`, root-owned, while `--user`
127	    writes into the invoking user's own home directory and needs no elevation at
128	    all. The scope flag alone decides this — never a separate "is this destructive"
129	    guess — so a user-scope item can never silently escalate to a root-run command.
130	    """
131	    return "sudo " if scope == "system" else ""

134	def _split_flatpak_item_id(item_id: str, expected_kind: Literal["ref", "remote", "mask"]) -> tuple[str, str]:
135	    """`(scope, name)` from a `flatpak:<kind>:<scope>:<name>` item id (packages/items.py).
136	
137	    `name` is the application id for a ref, the remote name for a remote, the pattern
138	    for a mask — none carries a `:` of its own: refs/remotes are dotted/alnum tokens
139	    and mask patterns are partial refs with `/` and `*` wildcards but never `:`
140	    (RESEARCH Standard Stack, verified live), so a fixed 3-colon split is exact rather
141	    than a heuristic (the `split(":", 3)` cap keeps any `/` inside a pattern intact).
142	    This is a legitimate use of a
143	    stable identity string (the same pattern `apt_sync._package_name` and
144	    `snap_sync._snap_name` already establish): the plan only ever carries `ItemDiff`s,
145	    not the richer item dataclasses, so converge() recovers scope/name from the id.
146	    """
147	    parts = item_id.split(":", 3)
148	    if len(parts) != 4 or parts[0] != "flatpak" or parts[1] != expected_kind:
149	        raise ValueError(f"not a flatpak {expected_kind} item id: {item_id!r}")
150	    _, _, scope, name = parts
151	    return scope, name

154	def _parse_flatpak_list(output: str) -> list[FlatpakItem]:
155	    """Parse `_FLATPAK_LIST_CMD`'s tab-separated output into `FlatpakItem`s.
156	
157	    A line whose `installation` field is neither `user` nor `system` (flatpak permits
158	    additional named installations beyond the two this item model represents) is
159	    skipped rather than guessed at — this project's own machines only ever use the
160	    two standard scopes (CONTEXT.md's live inventory), and a third would need its own
161	    modelling decision, not a silent default.
162	    """
163	    items: list[FlatpakItem] = []
164	    for line in _lines(output):
165	        fields = line.split("\t")
166	        if len(fields) != 4:
167	            continue
168	        application, version, origin, installation = fields
169	        scope: Literal["user", "system"]
170	        if installation == "user":
171	            scope = "user"
172	        elif installation == "system":
173	            scope = "system"
174	        else:
175	            continue
176	        items.append(FlatpakItem(application=application, version=version, origin=origin, scope=scope))
177	    return items

180	def _parse_flatpak_remotes(output: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"]) -> list[FlatpakRemoteItem]:
181	    """Parse one scope's `flatpak remotes --columns=name,url` output.
182	
183	    `scope` is a parameter, not a parsed column: unlike `flatpak list`, this command
184	    has no scope column of its own — the caller already knows which scope it asked
185	    about, because it chose the `--user`/`--system` flag (module docstring).
186	    """
187	    items: list[FlatpakRemoteItem] = []
188	    for line in _lines(output):
189	        fields = line.split("\t")
190	        if len(fields) != 2:
191	            continue
192	        name, url = fields
193	        items.append(FlatpakRemoteItem(name=name, url=url, scope=scope))
194	    return items

197	def _parse_flatpak_masks(output: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"]) -> list[FlatpakMaskItem]:
198	    """Parse one scope's `flatpak {--user|--system} mask` output into `FlatpakMaskItem`s.
199	
200	    Unlike the tab-separated list commands, `flatpak mask` prints each pattern on its
201	    own line prefixed with two leading spaces and no header (RESEARCH: verified live,
202	    Flatpak 1.14.6), so this strips leading/trailing whitespace per non-blank line
203	    rather than splitting on tabs. `scope` is a parameter, not a parsed column: the
204	    command has no scope column: the caller already chose the `--user`/`--system` flag
205	    (same reasoning as `_parse_flatpak_remotes`).
206	    """
207	    items: list[FlatpakMaskItem] = []
208	    for line in output.splitlines():
209	        pattern = line.strip()
210	        if not pattern:
211	            continue
212	        items.append(FlatpakMaskItem(pattern=pattern, scope=scope))
213	    return items

254	def _diff_flatpak_refs(source_items: Sequence[FlatpakItem], target_items: Sequence[FlatpakItem]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
255	    """One diff per ref `item_id` present on either side, source-then-target order —
256	    same shape as `PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_packages`/`snap_sync._diff_snap_items`.
257	    Scope already lives inside `item_id`, so an application installed in a different
258	    scope on each machine naturally produces one install-side entry and one
259	    remove-side entry here, never a single combined diff.
260	    """
261	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
262	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
263	
264	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
265	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
266	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
267	
268	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
269	    for item_id in seen:
270	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
271	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
272	
273	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
274	            diffs.append(_install_ref_diff(source_item))
275	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
276	            diffs.append(_remove_ref_diff(target_item))
277	        elif source_item is not None and target_item is not None and source_item.version != target_item.version:
278	            diffs.append(_version_mismatch_ref_diff(item_id, source_item, target_item))
279	        # else: present on both, same scope, equal version -> no diff.
280	
281	    return diffs

306	def _change_remote_diff(source_item: FlatpakRemoteItem, target_item: FlatpakRemoteItem) -> ItemDiff:
307	    """A remote present on both sides with the same name AND scope but a DIFFERING URL:
308	    converge the target's remote to the source's URL (decision 7).
309	
310	    A URL edit is a config change, so this is a `DiffAction.CHANGE` (default-ticked
311	    review group, install-direction), not a REMOVE+INSTALL churn — `_converge_remote`
312	    prefers `flatpak remote-modify --url`, which edits the entry in place and preserves
313	    the remote's other configuration (gpg key, filter, priority). Tagged
314	    `VERSION_MISMATCH` for the same reason apt config/source edits and snap
315	    revision/channel changes are (`apt_sync`/`snap_sync`): it is the "same identity,
316	    differing value" conflict class, the only `DiffClass` a CHANGE ever carries.
317	    """
318	    return ItemDiff(
319	        item_class=ItemClass.FLATPAK_REMOTE,
320	        diff_class=DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH,
321	        action=DiffAction.CHANGE,
322	        item_id=source_item.item_id,
323	        label=source_item.label(),
324	        detail=f"remote {source_item.name} url: {source_item.url} vs {target_item.url}",
325	    )

328	def _diff_flatpak_remotes(
329	    source_items: Sequence[FlatpakRemoteItem], target_items: Sequence[FlatpakRemoteItem]
330	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
331	    """One diff per remote `item_id` (name + scope) present on either side.
332	
333	    A remote present on both sides with the SAME name and scope but a DIFFERING URL is
334	    a `CHANGE` diff that converges the target to the source's URL (decision 7 /
335	    T-02-22): a same-name remote whose URL was silently not propagated is exactly the
336	    gap this closes. URL is the only field compared here — name and scope ARE the
337	    identity, so a difference in either produces two separate install/remove diffs, not
338	    a change (module docstring's scope-as-identity rule).
339	    """
340	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
341	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
342	
343	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
344	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
345	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
346	
347	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
348	    for item_id in seen:
349	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
350	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
351	
352	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
353	            diffs.append(_install_remote_diff(source_item))
354	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
355	            diffs.append(_remove_remote_diff(target_item))
356	        elif source_item is not None and target_item is not None and source_item.url != target_item.url:
357	            diffs.append(_change_remote_diff(source_item, target_item))
358	        # else: present on both, same url -> no diff.
359	
360	    return diffs

385	def _diff_flatpak_masks(
386	    source_items: Sequence[FlatpakMaskItem], target_items: Sequence[FlatpakMaskItem]
387	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
388	    """One diff per mask `item_id` (scope + pattern) present on either side (#208, D-10).
389	
390	    Pure membership, no `CHANGE`: a mask has no value to change, only presence — so
391	    source-has & target-lacks -> `INSTALL` (add the mask on target); target-has &
392	    source-lacks -> `REMOVE` (unmask on target); present on both -> no diff. A pattern
393	    edit therefore reads as remove-old + add-new and a user/system scope split as
394	    add + remove (scope is identity, same as refs/remotes), reported as found rather
395	    than normalised.
396	    """
397	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
398	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
399	
400	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
401	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
402	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
403	
404	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
405	    for item_id in seen:
406	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
407	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
408	
409	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
410	            diffs.append(_install_mask_diff(source_item))
411	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
412	            diffs.append(_remove_mask_diff(target_item))
413	        # else: present on both -> no diff (pure membership, no value to change).
414	
415	    return diffs

435	    pipeline (module docstring explains why the inherited apt-package-shaped one
436	    cannot express two ordered item classes); `accept_review()`, `apply()` and
437	    `execute()` are inherited unchanged.
438	    """

440	    name: ClassVar[str] = "flatpak_sync"
441	    manager_id: ClassVar[str] = "flatpak"

444	    # the enable flag in sync_jobs is needed for this slice.

451	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
452	        super().__init__(context)
453	        # Populated by plan()'s own capture/query step (post filter_inert) and
454	        # consulted by converge(): the base pipeline only ever hands converge() an
455	        # ItemDiff, whose item_id carries scope + name but not the source's origin
456	        # remote or a remote's URL — those have to come from somewhere else.
457	        self._source_refs_by_id: dict[str, FlatpakItem] = {}
458	        self._source_remotes_by_id: dict[str, FlatpakRemoteItem] = {}
459	        self._target_remotes_by_id: dict[str, FlatpakRemoteItem] = {}
460	        # (scope, name) pairs for remotes THIS RUN has already successfully added —
461	        # consulted by a ref install's remote-readiness guard alongside
462	        # `_target_remotes_by_id`, since a remote approved in the same run is not yet
463	        # present in the plan-time target query (D-14's whole point: it converges
464	        # first, in the SAME run, not in a prior one).
465	        self._converged_remote_scope_names: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()

467	    @override
468	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[FlatpakItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]

470	
471	        This job overrides `plan()` and never routes through `PackageSyncJob.
472	        diff_items`'s apt-package-shaped dispatch (module docstring), so widening this
473	        hook's item type here is safe: no code holding a `PackageSyncJob`-typed
474	        reference ever calls it expecting an `AptPackageItem` back — the same
475	        justification `SnapSyncJob.capture_source_items` documents.
476	        """
477	        result = await self.source.run_command(_FLATPAK_LIST_CMD)
478	        return _parse_flatpak_list(result.stdout)

480	    @override
481	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[FlatpakItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
482	        """The target's own `flatpak list --app` (same reasoning as `capture_source_items`)."""

484	        return _parse_flatpak_list(result.stdout)

522	        """Both scopes, one call each (D-10): masks are per-installation like remotes,

524	        """

526	        for scope in _SCOPES:
527	            masks.extend(await self._capture_source_masks(scope))

536	    @override
537	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
538	        """Load decision files -> capture -> query -> diff -> build review groups.
539	
540	        Read-only: only `flatpak list`/`flatpak remotes`/`flatpak mask` (both machines,
541	        both scopes) and a decision-file `cat` run here — no `flatpak install`/
542	        `uninstall`/`remote-add`/`remote-delete`/`mask` mutation before this returns.
543	        Caches the filtered source/target refs and remotes by id for `converge()` (see
544	        `__init__`); masks need no cache (pattern is fully in the item_id).
545	
546	        Diffs are ordered remotes -> refs -> masks in the returned `diffs` tuple — this
547	        job's own ordering stage, mirroring `apt_sync`'s key-before-source sort: a ref's
548	        `flatpak install` fails when its remote is not yet configured in that scope
549	        (D-14), and a mask applied before its refs could suppress an auto-pulled
550	        dependency of a ref being installed the same run (D-08). The base `apply()` loop
551	        converges `plan.diffs` in order, so this ordering is what enforces both.
552	        """
553	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
554	        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
555	
556	        source_refs = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
557	        target_refs = await filter_inert(await self.query_target_items(), target_decisions)
558	        source_remotes = await filter_inert(await self._capture_all_source_remotes(), source_decisions)
559	        target_remotes = await filter_inert(await self._query_all_target_remotes(), target_decisions)
560	        source_masks = await filter_inert(await self._capture_all_source_masks(), source_decisions)
561	        target_masks = await filter_inert(await self._query_all_target_masks(), target_decisions)
562	
563	        self._source_refs_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_refs}
564	        self._source_remotes_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_remotes}
565	        self._target_remotes_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_remotes}
566	
567	        remote_diffs = _diff_flatpak_remotes(source_remotes, target_remotes)
568	        ref_diffs = _diff_flatpak_refs(source_refs, target_refs)
569	        mask_diffs = _diff_flatpak_masks(source_masks, target_masks)
570	        # Ordering (D-08): remotes -> refs -> masks. A mask must land AFTER the refs so
571	        # it can never suppress an auto-pulled dependency of a ref being installed the
572	        # same run; converge() carries the pattern fully in the item_id, so masks (unlike
573	        # refs) need no source-side cache.
574	        diffs = (*remote_diffs, *ref_diffs, *mask_diffs)
575	
576	        groups = self._build_review_groups(diffs)
577	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=diffs, groups=groups)
578	
579	    @override
580	    async def converge(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
581	        """Add/install/remove/delete, dispatched by item class then action — the only
582	        D-06/D-14-safe verbs (module docstring). One item per invocation (D-27) so a
583	        single bad item cannot fail the whole batch. Every command is prefixed with
584	        `sudo` if and only if the item's own scope is `system` (`_sudo_prefix`,
585	        T-02-23): a `--user` command never runs as root, and a `--system` command
586	        always does, regardless of which of the four verbs it is.
587	        """
588	        if diff.item_class == ItemClass.FLATPAK_REMOTE:
589	            return await self._converge_remote(diff)
590	        if diff.item_class == ItemClass.FLATPAK_REF:
591	            return await self._converge_ref(diff)
592	        if diff.item_class == ItemClass.FLATPAK_MASK:
593	            return await self._converge_mask(diff)
594	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(
595	            f"FlatpakSyncJob.converge: unsupported item class {diff.item_class.value!r} for {diff.label}"
596	        )
597	
598	    async def _converge_remote(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
599	        scope, name = _split_flatpak_item_id(diff.item_id, "remote")
600	        scope_flag = _scope_flag(scope)
601	        sudo = _sudo_prefix(scope)
602	
603	        if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL:
604	            source_item = self._source_remotes_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
605	            if source_item is None:
606	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(
607	                    f"no captured source remote for {diff.label} (item_id={diff.item_id!r}); "
608	                    "was plan() run before converge()?"
609	                )
610	            cmd = (
611	                f"{sudo}flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists {scope_flag} "
612	                f"{shlex.quote(name)} {shlex.quote(source_item.url)}"
613	            )
614	            result = await self.target.run_command(
615	                cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"add {scope} flatpak remote {name} ({source_item.url})"
616	            )
617	            if result.success:
618	                self._converged_remote_scope_names.add((scope, name))
619	            return result
620	
621	        if diff.action == DiffAction.CHANGE:
622	            source_item = self._source_remotes_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
623	            if source_item is None:
624	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(
625	                    f"no captured source remote for {diff.label} (item_id={diff.item_id!r}); "
626	                    "was plan() run before converge()?"
627	                )
628	            # `remote-modify --url` edits the existing entry in place (the remote is
629	            # present on both sides by construction of a CHANGE diff), preserving its
630	            # other config and avoiding the ref-origin disruption a delete+re-add would
631	            # cause. No need to record it in `_converged_remote_scope_names`: the remote
632	            # already exists on the target, so ref-readiness (`_remote_ready_on_target`)
633	            # is already satisfied via the plan-time target query.
634	            cmd = f"{sudo}flatpak remote-modify {scope_flag} --url={shlex.quote(source_item.url)} {shlex.quote(name)}"
635	            return await self.target.run_command(
636	                cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"repoint {scope} flatpak remote {name} at {source_item.url}"
637	            )
638	
639	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
640	            cmd = f"{sudo}flatpak remote-delete {scope_flag} {shlex.quote(name)}"
641	            return await self.target.run_command(
642	                cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"delete {scope} flatpak remote {name}"
643	            )
644	
645	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(
646	            f"FlatpakSyncJob.converge: unsupported action {diff.action.value!r} for a flatpak remote ({diff.label})"
647	        )
648	
649	    async def _converge_ref(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
650	        scope, application = _split_flatpak_item_id(diff.item_id, "ref")
651	        scope_flag = _scope_flag(scope)
652	        sudo = _sudo_prefix(scope)
653	
654	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
655	            cmd = f"{sudo}flatpak uninstall -y {scope_flag} {shlex.quote(application)}"
656	            return await self.target.run_command(
657	                cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"uninstall {scope} flatpak {application}"
658	            )
659	
660	        if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL:
661	            source_item = self._source_refs_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
662	            if source_item is None:
663	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(
664	                    f"no captured source ref for {diff.label} (item_id={diff.item_id!r}); "
665	                    "was plan() run before converge()?"
666	                )
667	            if not self._remote_ready_on_target(scope, source_item.origin):
668	                # T-02-24: refuse rather than issue an install flatpak will reject.
669	                raise ConvergeItemFailed(
670	                    f"install of {application} refused: origin remote {source_item.origin!r} ({scope}) is "
671	                    "neither already configured on the target nor among this run's successfully-added "
672	                    "remotes (D-14)"
673	                )
674	            cmd = f"{sudo}flatpak install -y {scope_flag} {shlex.quote(source_item.origin)} {shlex.quote(application)}"
675	            return await self.target.run_command(
676	                cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"install {scope} flatpak {application} from {source_item.origin}"
677	            )
678	
679	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(
680	            f"FlatpakSyncJob.converge: unsupported action {diff.action.value!r} for a flatpak ref ({diff.label}) "
681	            "— version mismatches are report_only per D-04 and never reach converge()"
682	        )
683	
684	    async def _converge_mask(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
685	        """Add or remove one flatpak mask (#208, D-10). Scope + pattern come entirely
686	        from the item_id (no source-side lookup, unlike refs/remotes): a mask is a pure
687	        pattern, so `_split_flatpak_item_id(..., "mask")` recovers everything converge
688	        needs. `sudo` iff system scope (`_sudo_prefix`), the pattern `shlex.quote`d.
689	
690	        Idempotent for the add direction (masking an already-present pattern exits 0);
691	        the remove direction only ever targets a pattern the target scope actually
692	        reported (it came from a REMOVE diff against the target's own mask set), so
693	        `mask --remove` never hits the exit-1 non-existent-pattern path. Exit code alone
694	        decides pass/fail (D-27).
695	        """
696	        scope, pattern = _split_flatpak_item_id(diff.item_id, "mask")
697	        scope_flag = _scope_flag(scope)
698	        sudo = _sudo_prefix(scope)
699	
700	        if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL:
701	            cmd = f"{sudo}flatpak {scope_flag} mask {shlex.quote(pattern)}"
702	            return await self.target.run_command(
703	                cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"mask {scope} flatpak pattern {pattern}"
704	            )
705	
706	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
707	            cmd = f"{sudo}flatpak {scope_flag} mask --remove {shlex.quote(pattern)}"
708	            return await self.target.run_command(
709	                cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"unmask {scope} flatpak pattern {pattern}"
710	            )
711	
712	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(
713	            f"FlatpakSyncJob.converge: unsupported action {diff.action.value!r} for a flatpak mask ({diff.label})"
714	        )

716	    def _remote_ready_on_target(self, scope: str, origin: str) -> bool:
717	        """Whether `origin` is usable as a ref's remote in `scope`: already present on
718	        the target per the plan-time query, or successfully added earlier in THIS run
719	        (T-02-24's guard — see `converge()`'s module docstring).
720	        """
721	        remote_id = f"flatpak:remote:{scope}:{origin}"
722	        if remote_id in self._target_remotes_by_id:
723	            return True
724	        return (scope, origin) in self._converged_remote_scope_names
725	
726	    async def _system_scope_in_play(self) -> bool:
727	        """Whether ANY system-scope ref, remote or mask exists on either machine — the
728	        gate for `validate()`'s sudo check (T-02-23, ASVS V4): user-scope flatpak
729	        operations need no root at all, so this job never asks for a privilege it
730	        will not use. A system-scope mask on either machine (#208, D-07) writes into
731	        `/var/lib/flatpak` just like a system remote, so it too requires target sudo.
732	        """
733	        if any(item.scope == "system" for item in await self.capture_source_items()):
734	            return True
735	        if any(item.scope == "system" for item in await self.query_target_items()):
736	            return True
737	        if await self._capture_source_remotes("system"):
738	            return True
739	        if await self._query_target_remotes("system"):
740	            return True
741	        if await self._capture_source_masks("system"):
742	            return True
743	        return bool(await self._query_target_masks("system"))

745	    @override
746	    async def validate(self) -> list[ValidationError]:
747	        """`flatpak --version` on both ends — a missing binary is a reported
748	        validation error naming flatpak's absence (it ships in no default Ubuntu

3	
4	Two detectors, both run on the SOURCE:
5	
6	- apt packages in the source's `apt-mark showmanual` set whose SOURCE `apt-cache policy`

8	  registered with any configured repository.

11	  script dropped there, bypassing apt entirely.
12	
13	Both were previously folded into `apt_sync`. D-18 pulls them into their own job with its
14	own enable flag, because half of what they cover is not apt's business at all (unowned
15	files under `/usr/local`/`/opt`), and folding it into `apt_sync` meant disabling apt
16	silently disabled manual-install detection with nothing telling the user. This job does

18	clean — it never imports `apt_sync` (D-18).

84	# D-19's bounded unowned-install scan: top-level entries of `/usr/local` and `/opt`, plus
85	# the immediate children of `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/local/lib` — one batched
86	# `find <dir...> -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` covers all four, since `find` applies the same
87	# depth options to every starting path it is given. Enough to NAME a finding (D-18), never
88	# enough to walk an entire tree — the item is decided on, not replicated (deferred ideas,
89	# CONTEXT.md). Owned by this job now, no longer shared with apt_sync (D-18).
90	_UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS = ("/usr/local", "/opt", "/usr/local/bin", "/usr/local/lib")
91	
92	# Matches one `dpkg -S` "owned" line: `<package>[,<package>...]: <path>`. A path dpkg does
93	# not own produces no such line at all (its "no path found" diagnostic goes to stderr,
94	# which this scan never inspects) — absence from stdout is the only signal
95	# `_owned_paths_from_dpkg_s` needs. A private copy of apt_sync's identical regex: D-18
96	# keeps ownership clean by NOT importing apt_sync, and this parser is small enough that
97	# one duplicated line is cheaper than a shared-core coupling.
98	_DPKG_S_OWNED_RE = re.compile(r"^[^:]+:\s+(?P<path>/\S.*)$")
99	
100	
101	def _lines(output: str) -> list[str]:
102	    """Non-blank, stripped lines — the shape every `apt-mark`/`find` list command this
103	    module runs produces. A private copy of apt_sync's identical helper (D-18)."""
104	    return [line.strip() for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
105

107	def _packages_with_no_candidate(policy_output: str) -> set[str]:
108	    """Parse a multi-package `apt-cache policy <name...>` run: names whose `Candidate:`
109	    line reads `(none)`. Each package's block starts with an unindented `<name>:` header
110	    line, per `apt-cache policy`'s documented output shape. A private copy of apt_sync's
111	    identical parser (D-18): apt_sync keeps its own for `collect_unavailable_item_ids`
112	    (D-25 REPO_UNAVAILABLE, a distinct concern about the TARGET's repos), so both jobs own
113	    the parser they need without either importing the other.
114	    """
115	    no_candidate: set[str] = set()
116	    current: str | None = None
117	    for line in policy_output.splitlines():
118	        if line and not line[0].isspace() and line.endswith(":"):
119	            current = line[:-1]
120	            continue
121	        if current is None:
122	            continue
123	        stripped = line.strip()
124	        if stripped.startswith("Candidate:"):
125	            if stripped.removeprefix("Candidate:").strip() == "(none)":
126	                no_candidate.add(current)
127	            current = None
128	    return no_candidate
129	
130	
131	def _owned_paths_from_dpkg_s(output: str) -> frozenset[str]:
132	    """Every path `dpkg -S` reports as owned, parsed from its stdout alone (D-19's
133	    unowned-install scan). A queried path dpkg does NOT own is simply absent from this set
134	    — its "no path found matching pattern" diagnostic is a stderr message this scan never
135	    reads, so a batched multi-path `dpkg -S` degrades cleanly even when some paths are
136	    unowned and others are not. A private copy of apt_sync's identical parser (D-18).
137	    """
138	    owned: set[str] = set()
139	    for line in output.splitlines():
140	        match = _DPKG_S_OWNED_RE.match(line)
141	        if match:
142	            owned.add(match.group("path"))
143	    return frozenset(owned)

152	    registered install snippet verbatim (D-20); the unreproducible finalize hook the base
153	    leaves as a no-op is implemented here.
154	    """

160	    # in sync_jobs is needed. D-32 forbids an empty placeholder config SECTION, so there is
161	    # no `manual_installs_sync:` block in default-config.yaml, but the in-code CONFIG_SCHEMA
