169	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
170	        super().__init__(context)
171	        # Guards `_finalize_unreproducible` to run at most once per run. `after_review()`
172	        # calls it (so the pushed registry includes on-the-fly snippets), then the base
173	        # `apply()` calls it again; the second call is a no-op so a snippet's `authored_at`
174	        # is stamped exactly once and the source and pushed target registries stay identical.
175	        self._unreproducible_finalized = False
176	
177	    # -- after-review snippet push (D-23) -----------------------------------------------
178	
179	    @override
180	    async def after_review(self) -> None:
181	        """Push the install-snippet registry to the target after this job's review and
182	        before `apply()` replays any snippet (D-23), then promote each on-the-fly-authored
183	        item so it is APPLIED — not merely transported — the same run.
184	
185	        Finalize-then-push-then-promote: `_finalize_unreproducible` persists this run's
186	        authored snippets into the SOURCE registry first (idempotent — `apply()` calls it
187	        again as a no-op), then `_push_snippet_registry` copies that file to the target,
188	        and finally `_promote_authored_snippets_to_install` reclassifies each authored
189	        item's diff `REPORT_ONLY -> INSTALL` decided `APPLY` so the unchanged base
190	        `apply()` converges it this run rather than the next one. Promotion runs AFTER the
191	        push so the target already holds the snippet the replay reads. The push depends on
192	        no other job: it moves the file itself and reads neither `config_sync` nor
193	        `folder_sync` state, so disabling either cannot break snippet delivery.
194	        """
195	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
196	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
197	        await self._finalize_unreproducible(self._accepted_plan, self._accepted_outcome)
198	        await self._push_snippet_registry()
199	        self._promote_authored_snippets_to_install()
200	
201	    def _promote_authored_snippets_to_install(self) -> None:
202	        """Reclassify every on-the-fly-authored item's diff `REPORT_ONLY -> INSTALL` and
203	        force its decision to `APPLY`, so the unchanged base `apply()` — which converges
204	        only APPLY-decided, non-`REPORT_ONLY` diffs (`sync_core.py` apply_diffs filter) —
205	        replays the freshly authored snippet THIS run, closing the one-run-too-late gap.
206	
207	        Called from `after_review()` only after the authored snippets are persisted to the
208	        source registry and pushed to the target, so the target holds the snippet by the
209	        time the promoted diff converges. The add-snippet review path records no decision
210	        for the item (`packages.review._review_unreproducible_group`), so the decision must
211	        be forced here in addition to reclassifying the action.
212	
213	        Mutates only in-memory accepted state (a `dataclasses.replace` of the frozen plan
214	        and outcome), so it is safe under dry-run: `apply()`'s dry-run branch previews a
215	        would-install line and issues no converge, preserving ADR-014.
216	        """
217	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
218	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
219	        outcome = self._accepted_outcome
220	        if not outcome.snippets:
221	            return
222	
223	        plan = self._accepted_plan
224	        authored = frozenset(outcome.snippets)
225	        new_diffs = tuple(
226	            replace(diff, action=DiffAction.INSTALL)
227	            if diff.item_id in authored and diff.action is DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
228	            else diff
229	            for diff in plan.diffs
230	        )
231	        new_decisions = dict(outcome.decisions)
232	        for item_id in authored:
233	            new_decisions[item_id] = Decision.APPLY
234	
235	        self._accepted_plan = replace(plan, diffs=new_diffs)
236	        self._accepted_outcome = replace(outcome, decisions=new_decisions)

238	    async def _push_snippet_registry(self) -> None:
239	        """Copy the source's `~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml` to the target's
240	        own copy under the SSH user's home, mirroring `config_sync._copy_config_to_target`'s
241	        `mkdir -p` -> `echo $HOME` -> `send_file` shape.
242	
243	        `send_file` writes plain SFTP as the SSH user, always under that user's home
244	        (`~/.config/pc-switcher`) — never `/etc` — which is exactly where the registry
245	        belongs, so no `sudo install` staging is needed. A no-op if the source has no
246	        registry file yet (a user who has never authored a snippet) and under dry-run
247	        (ADR-014: a rehearsal transfers nothing).
248	
249	        The push is a WHOLE-FILE overwrite (no per-entry merge). Before it runs,
250	        `_guard_registry_overwrite` compares the target's current registry against the
251	        source's on-disk file (decision 9): a purely additive push (source superset of
252	        target) proceeds silently, while one that would lose or change a target entry
253	        requires explicit confirmation and otherwise aborts the run.
254	        """
255	        if self.context.dry_run:
256	            return
257	
258	        source_path = Path.home() / SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH
259	        if not source_path.exists():
260	            return
261	
262	        await self._guard_registry_overwrite(source_path)
263	
264	        mkdir = await self.target.run_command(
265	            f"mkdir -p {CONFIG_REMOTE_DIR}", mutates="create the pc-switcher config directory on the target"
266	        )
267	        if not mkdir.success:
268	            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to create config directory on target: {mkdir.stderr}")
269	
270	        # send_file needs an absolute remote path, so expand the target's ~ once.
271	        home = await self.target.run_command("echo $HOME")
272	        if not home.success:
273	            raise RuntimeError("Failed to get home directory on target")
274	        absolute_remote_path = f"{home.stdout.strip()}/{SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH}"
275	        await self.target.send_file(
276	            source_path, absolute_remote_path, mutates="push the install-snippet registry to the target"
277	        )
278	
279	    async def _guard_registry_overwrite(self, source_path: Path) -> None:
280	        """Gate the wholesale `package-snippets.yaml` overwrite on the loss/change of any
281	        target entry (decision 9).
282	
283	        The source's on-disk file (the exact bytes about to be sent) is compared against
284	        the target's current registry per `item_id`. The push is purely additive when the
285	        source is a superset of the target — every target entry is present in the source
286	        with an identical body — in which case it proceeds silently, as before. Otherwise
287	        the target holds an entry that a wholesale overwrite would LOSE (absent from the
288	        source) or CHANGE (a differing body); the user is shown exactly which entries and
289	        must confirm. Declining, or a non-interactive run that cannot confirm, aborts the
290	        whole sync (`SyncAbortedByUser`) so the user can consolidate the two registries by
291	        hand and re-run — the tool never silently discards a snippet only the target has.
292	        """
293	        source_snippets = load_snippets_from_text(source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
294	        target_snippets = await SnippetRegistry(self.target).load()
295	
296	        lost = [snippet for item_id, snippet in target_snippets.items() if item_id not in source_snippets]
297	        changed = [
298	            (snippet, source_snippets[item_id])
299	            for item_id, snippet in target_snippets.items()
300	            if item_id in source_snippets and source_snippets[item_id].body != snippet.body
301	        ]
302	        if not lost and not changed:
303	            return  # purely additive — source is a superset of the target
304	
305	        assert self.context.confirmer is not None, (
306	            "a non-additive snippet registry overwrite needs a confirmer to gate it"
307	        )
308	        approved = await self.context.confirmer.confirm(
309	            title="Snippet registry overwrite is not purely additive",
310	            message=self._render_overwrite_diff(lost, changed),
311	            # No override flag exists: a lossy overwrite is only ever approved by a human
312	            # answering the prompt, so `allow=False` makes any non-interactive run refuse
313	            # (and thus abort) rather than silently overwrite.
314	            allow=False,
315	            allow_flag="manual registry consolidation",
316	            log_extra={"job": self.name, "host": "source"},
317	        )
318	        if not approved:
319	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(
320	                "snippet registry overwrite declined: the target holds snippet entries "
321	                "absent from or differing in the source that a wholesale push would lose "
322	                "or change; consolidate the two registries by hand and re-run"
323	            )
324	
325	    @staticmethod
326	    def _render_overwrite_diff(lost: list[Snippet], changed: list[tuple[Snippet, Snippet]]) -> str:
327	        """Rich-markup body naming every target entry a wholesale push would lose or change.
328	
329	        Every snippet field is untrusted package-manager/user text, so each is
330	        `rich.markup.escape`d before it reaches the confirmer's `Panel` — a body or label
331	        containing `[...]` must not be parsed as console markup (T-02-02).
332	        """
333	
334	        def body_lines(body: str, indent: str) -> list[str]:
335	            return [f"{indent}{escape(line)}" for line in (body.splitlines() or [""])]
336	
337	        lines = ["The target's snippet registry holds entries this overwrite would discard or replace:", ""]
338	        for snippet in lost:
339	            lines.append(f"  LOST     {escape(snippet.label)}  ({escape(snippet.item_id)})")
340	            lines.extend(body_lines(snippet.body, "             "))
341	        for target_snippet, source_snippet in changed:
342	            lines.append(f"  CHANGED  {escape(target_snippet.label)}  ({escape(target_snippet.item_id)})")
343	            lines.append("             target (to be replaced):")
344	            lines.extend(body_lines(target_snippet.body, "               "))
345	            lines.append("             source (incoming):")
346	            lines.extend(body_lines(source_snippet.body, "               "))
347	        lines += [
348	            "",
349	            "Continuing overwrites the target's registry wholesale. Decline to abort and "
350	            "consolidate the two registries by hand.",
351	        ]
352	        return "\n".join(lines)

354	    # -- Detection (D-18/D-19), all on the source ---------------------------------------
355	
356	    async def _scan_no_candidate_apt_packages(self, manual_names: Sequence[str]) -> list[UnreproducibleItem]:
357	        """D-18: manually-installed packages whose SOURCE's own `apt-cache` has no
358	        candidate at all — installed via `dpkg -i` of a bare `.deb`, never registered with
359	        any configured repository. Runs the job's OWN `apt-cache policy` (D-18), never
360	        apt_sync's.
361	        """
362	        if not manual_names:
363	            return []
364	
365	        quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(name) for name in manual_names)
366	        result = await self.source.run_command(f"apt-cache policy {quoted}")
367	        no_candidate = _packages_with_no_candidate(result.stdout)
368	        return [
369	            UnreproducibleItem(origin="apt-no-candidate", identifier=name, label=f"{name} (no apt candidate)")
370	            for name in sorted(no_candidate)
371	        ]
372	
373	    async def _scan_unowned_installs(self) -> list[UnreproducibleItem]:
374	        """D-18/D-19: paths under `/usr/local` and `/opt` that no dpkg package owns —
375	        software an install script dropped there directly, bypassing apt entirely.
376	
377	        One batched `find` over `_UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS` names every candidate path, then one
378	        batched `dpkg -S` over those candidates decides ownership; a path absent from the
379	        `dpkg -S` output is unowned. Both steps run on the SOURCE (D-18) — a fact about
380	        what the source machine has installed, not the target.
381	        """
382	        quoted_roots = " ".join(shlex.quote(root) for root in _UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS)
383	        listing = await self.source.run_command(f"find {quoted_roots} -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 2>/dev/null")
384	        candidates = _lines(listing.stdout)
385	        if not candidates:
386	            return []
387	
388	        quoted_paths = " ".join(shlex.quote(path) for path in candidates)
389	        ownership = await self.source.run_command(f"dpkg -S {quoted_paths}")
390	        owned = _owned_paths_from_dpkg_s(ownership.stdout)
391	
392	        return [
393	            UnreproducibleItem(origin="unowned-path", identifier=path, label=path)
394	            for path in sorted(set(candidates) - owned)
395	        ]

397	    # -- plan() / converge() ------------------------------------------------------------
398	
399	    @override
400	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[UnreproducibleItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
401	        """The source's unreproducible items: apt-no-candidate packages plus unowned
402	        `/usr/local`/`/opt` installs (D-18). `apt-mark showmanual` runs once here and its
403	        result feeds the no-candidate scan.
404	
405	        This job overrides `plan()` and never routes through `PackageSyncJob.diff_items`'s
406	        apt-package-shaped dispatch, so widening this hook's item type is safe (same
407	        reasoning as `SnapSyncJob.capture_source_items`).
408	        """
409	        manual = await self.source.run_command("apt-mark showmanual")
410	        manual_names = _lines(manual.stdout)
411	        return [
412	            *await self._scan_no_candidate_apt_packages(manual_names),
413	            *await self._scan_unowned_installs(),
414	        ]
415	
416	    @override
417	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[UnreproducibleItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
418	        """No target-side manifest exists for unreproducible items: they are always
419	        source-held (they describe what the SOURCE machine has installed), and convergence
420	        is driven by the shared snippet registry, not by a diff against target state. The
421	        empty result keeps the abstract hook satisfied without a meaningless target query.
422	        """
423	        return []
424	
425	    @override
426	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
427	        """Detect -> filter inert -> diff against the SOURCE's snippet registry. Read-only.
428	
429	        An item already recorded machine-specific on the SOURCE is dropped by

1	"""Per-action confirmation gate behind `--confirm-each-command`.
2	
3	A package sync run converges dozens of small mutating commands — `apt-get install`,
4	`snap remove`, `sudo install` into `/etc/apt`, an SFTP push of the snippet registry — each
5	of which was approved only in aggregate, as a ticked line in a batched review. This gate
6	inserts one prompt before every single one of them, showing the EXACT operation about to
7	happen: the literal shell command as it will be passed to the shell, or the local path and
8	remote destination of a file transfer. Nothing is paraphrased or reconstructed for display,
9	because a display string that differs from what runs is worse than no display at all.
10	
11	Distinct from `pcswitcher.confirmer.Confirmer`, which gates ONE coarse decision per run
12	(first-sync overwrite, out-of-order topology) and falls back to an `--allow-*` flag when
13	nobody is there to answer. This gate has no such fallback and never auto-proceeds: it is
14	opt-in per run and refused outright without a TTY (`cli.sync`), because a gate that
15	auto-proceeds when unanswerable is precisely the failure it exists to prevent.
16	
17	Two outcomes only, with no default (the user must type one): proceed, or abort the whole
18	sync. There is deliberately no "skip this command" — a single reviewed item can span
19	several commands (apt source stage-then-promote, snap install-then-switch-channel), so
20	skipping one of them leaves that item half-applied, which is a worse state than either
21	finishing it or stopping.
22	
23	Generic on purpose, and invoked from exactly one place: `pcswitcher.executor`. Any caller
24	— job, orchestrator, helper — gates a write by passing `mutates="..."` to the executor
25	method it already uses, so there is no second API to remember and no per-job wiring. The
26	executor supplies `job` (from its `active_job` context variable) and `host` (from which
27	executor it is). Today only the package sync jobs pass `mutates`; `folder_sync` is #209.
28	"""
29	
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import logging
33	from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
34	
35	from rich.console import Console
36	from rich.panel import Panel
37	from rich.prompt import Prompt
38	from rich.text import Text
39	
40	from pcswitcher.confirmer import PausableUI
41	from pcswitcher.models import Host, SyncAbortedByUser
42	
43	__all__ = ["StepGate", "TerminalUIStepGate"]
44	
45	_PROCEED = "p"
46	_ABORT = "a"
47	
48	
49	@runtime_checkable
50	class StepGate(Protocol):
51	    """A per-action confirmation gate: show one pending modification, block, decide."""
52	
53	    async def confirm_action(self, *, job: str, host: Host, description: str, command: str) -> None:
54	        """Show a pending modification and block until the user decides.
55	
56	        Args:
57	            job: Name of the job about to modify something (panel heading, log context).
58	            host: Which machine the modification lands on.
59	            description: Short human phrase for what this achieves ("install firefox").
60	            command: The operation VERBATIM — the shell command as it will be executed, or
61	                a `send_file <local> -> <remote>` rendering for a transfer.
62	
63	        Returns:
64	            None when the user chose to proceed.
65	
66	        Raises:
67	            SyncAbortedByUser: The user aborted, or the prompt could not be answered
68	                (EOF / Ctrl-C). Never swallowed into a silent "proceed".
69	        """
70	        ...
71	
72	
73	class TerminalUIStepGate:
74	    """`StepGate` backed by the Rich console and the live `TerminalUI`.
75	
76	    Pauses the live display around the blocking prompt for the same reason
77	    `TerminalUIConfirmer` does — a Rich `Live` and a `Prompt.ask` cannot share the
78	    terminal — and resumes it in a `finally` so the display is handed back even when the
79	    prompt raises.
80	    """
81	
82	    def __init__(
83	        self,
84	        console: Console,
85	        ui: PausableUI,
86	        *,
87	        logger: logging.Logger | None = None,
88	    ) -> None:
89	        self._console = console
90	        self._ui = ui
91	        self._logger = logger if logger is not None else logging.getLogger("pcswitcher.step_gate")
92	
93	    async def confirm_action(self, *, job: str, host: Host, description: str, command: str) -> None:
94	        extra = {"job": job, "host": host.value}
95	
96	        # Body is assembled as a `Text`, never a markup string: `command` is arbitrary
97	        # content (package names, file paths, snippet bodies) and a stray `[` in it would
98	        # otherwise be parsed as Rich markup and raise mid-prompt.
99	        body = Text()
100	        body.append(f"{job} → {host.value}\n", style="bold")
101	        body.append(f"{description}\n\n", style="dim")
102	        body.append(command, style="bold")
103	
104	        self._ui.pause()
105	        try:
106	            self._console.print()
107	            self._console.print(Panel(body, title="Confirm modification", border_style="yellow"))
108	            self._console.print()
109	            # No `default=`: the user must type a choice. An accidental Enter re-prompts
110	            # rather than picking either outcome for them.
111	            response = Prompt.ask(
112	                f"[bold]Run this?[/bold] [{_PROCEED}] proceed  [{_ABORT}] abort sync",
113	                choices=[_PROCEED, _ABORT],
114	                show_choices=False,
115	            )
116	        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt) as exc:
117	            # Unanswerable is not approval: the same rule the review applies to Ctrl-C.
118	            self._logger.warning("Confirmation prompt interrupted; aborting sync", extra=extra)
119	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(f"{job}: confirmation prompt interrupted before {description}") from exc
120	        finally:
121	            self._ui.resume()
122	
123	        if response == _ABORT:
124	            self._logger.warning("Aborted by user at: %s", description, extra=extra)
125	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(f"{job}: aborted by user before {description} on {host.value}")
126	        self._logger.debug("Confirmed: %s", description, extra=extra)

uv run python - <<'EOF'
import ast, pathlib
files = [
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_snap_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_flatpak_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_manual_installs_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_items.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_review.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_state.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_sync_core.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_sync_candidate_selection.py",
 "tests/unit/test_step_gate.py",
 "tests/unit/orchestrator/test_snap_autorefresh_hold.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_folder_sync.py",
 "tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py",
]
for f in files:
    p = pathlib.Path(f)
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"MISSING {f}"); continue
    tree = ast.parse(p.read_text())
    print(f"\n===== {f} =====")
    def walk(node, cls=None):
        for n in node.body:
            if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef):
                d = ast.get_docstring(n) or ""
                print(f"  ## {n.name}: {d.strip().splitlines()[0] if d else ''}")
                walk(n, n.name)
            elif isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and n.name.startswith("test"):
                d = ast.get_docstring(n) or ""
                first = " ".join(d.strip().split())[:220] if d else ""
                print(f"    - {n.name} (L{n.lineno}): {first}")
    walk(tree)
EOF

async def test_probe_apt_hold_skip_always_next_run() -> None:

# Phase 02 — package sync scenario/coverage matrix

Requirement-derived scenario enumeration for the four package jobs, mapped to pytest coverage. Branches come from ADR-020, 02-CONTEXT.md (D-01…D-33), 02-208-HOLD-MASK-REPLICATION.md and docs/jobs/package-sync.md — not from code paths, though code was read to decide what actually happens.

## Legend

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| U | covered by a unit test that asserts this branch |
| V | covered by the VM integration suite |
| P | partial — a neighbouring test exists, this branch is not asserted |
| — | no coverage |
| ‼ | verified defect or verified requirement gap (probed this session) |

Test file shorthand: `apt` = tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py · `snap` = test_snap_sync.py · `flat` = test_flatpak_sync.py · `man` = test_manual_installs_sync.py · `core` = test_package_sync_core.py · `rev` = test_package_review.py · `state` = test_package_state.py · `items` = test_package_items.py · `fold` = test_folder_sync.py · `hold` = tests/unit/orchestrator/test_snap_autorefresh_hold.py · `gate` = tests/unit/test_step_gate.py · `cfg` = tests/unit/orchestrator/test_config_system.py · `exit` = test_session_status_from_job_results.py · `INT` = tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py

## A. apt packages — presence and version diff (D-03, D-04, D-25)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | On source's manual set, absent on target, candidate exists | MISSING_ON_TARGET → INSTALL, default-ticked | U V | core:`test_missing_on_target_yields_install`, apt:`test_diff_yields_exactly_two_missing_items`, INT:`test_apt_sync_installs_missing_package` |
| A2 | On source, absent on target, target repos offer no candidate | REPO_UNAVAILABLE → REPORT_ONLY, never an install | U | core:`test_missing_and_unavailable_yields_repo_unavailable_not_install`, apt:`test_no_candidate_package_is_reported_not_installed` |
| A3 | On target's manual set only | EXTRA_ON_TARGET → REMOVE, own unticked group | U | core:`test_extra_on_target_yields_remove`, apt:`test_extra_on_target_yields_extra_on_target_remove` |
| A4 | Present both, equal version | no diff at all | U | core:`test_equal_versions_yields_no_diff` |
| A5 | Present both, versions differ | VERSION_MISMATCH → REPORT_ONLY naming both versions; never force-converged | U | core:`test_version_mismatch_yields_report_only_with_both_versions` |
| A6 | Version ordering (epoch, tilde, revision) | decided by `dpkg --compare-versions`, never string compare | U | items:`TestCompareDebVersions` (incl. real-dpkg cross-check) |
| A7 | Package pinned on target via preferences.d | HELD_OR_PINNED REPORT_ONLY echo on the package | U | core:`test_pin_fact_yields_held_or_pinned_distinguishable_from_a_hold_item`, apt:`test_preferences_d_pin_surfaces_with_pin_mechanism_and_filename` |
| A8 | Package held on target | install/upgrade action suppressed, no package-level report | U | core:`test_target_hold_only_yields_apt_hold_remove_and_suppresses_package_action`, apt:`test_held_package_yields_hold_item_not_duplicate_held_or_pinned_report` |
| A9 | Package pinned *and* a hold exists for another package | pin echo and hold item coexist, stay distinguishable | U | apt:`test_pin_still_yields_report_only_echo_alongside_a_hold_item` |
| A10 | Dependency-only package (not in `apt-mark showmanual`) | never in the manifest → never installed, never removed, never reported | P | implicit in capture (`showmanual` only); no test asserts an auto-installed package is invisible. **This is the mechanism the user's example 1 depends on.** |
| A11 | Same package is no-candidate on source *and* missing on target | surfaces twice: `manual_installs_sync` unreproducible item + `apt_sync` REPO_UNAVAILABLE report | — | no test; two managers describe one package in two reviews |
| A12 | `apt-mark showmanual` empty on a machine | empty manifest, no crash, no mass removal | P | `_resolve_versions` early-returns; no test for the empty-source→remove-everything shape |
| A13 | Version resolution source | `dpkg-query`, never `apt list --installed` | U | apt:`test_dpkg_query_used_not_apt_list_installed` |

## B. apt holds (#208 D1–D6)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Held on source, not target | `apt:hold:<pkg>` INSTALL → `sudo apt-mark hold` | U | apt:`test_source_held_yields_install_hold_item_and_converge_runs_apt_mark_hold`, core:`test_source_hold_only_yields_apt_hold_install` |
| B2 | Held on target, not source | REMOVE → `sudo apt-mark unhold`, unticked removal group | U | apt:`test_target_held_only_yields_remove_unhold_item` |
| B3 | Held on both / neither | no hold diff | U | apt:`test_held_on_both_yields_no_hold_diff`, core:`test_held_on_both_yields_no_diff` |
| B4 | Hold identity is distinct from package identity | two separate review items for one package | U | apt:`test_held_package_yields_hold_item_not_duplicate_held_or_pinned_report` |
| B5 | Review verb | group/entry read "hold"/"unhold", never "install"/"remove" | — | **no test asserts the group title or `action_label` for APT_HOLD/SNAP_HOLD/FLATPAK_MASK** — the crux of #208 D3 |
| B6 | Hold converges after the package install in the same run (D8) | install lands before its hold | — | snap has the equivalent test; apt does not |
| B7 | Hold approved for a package whose install was skipped (D6) | `apt-mark hold` on an absent package → normal per-item failure | — | no test; actual `apt-mark` exit behaviour for an unknown package unverified |
| B8 | skip-always on a hold item | DecisionEntry written on the holder's machine | U | apt:`test_skip_always_on_a_hold_writes_the_decision_file` |
| B9 | skip-always on a hold item, next run | item inert, no diff | ‼ | **BROKEN — verified.** `collect_hold_sets()` output never passes `filter_inert`, so the hold diff is re-emitted every run despite the recorded decision |
| B10 | Holds drive no `apt-get -s` simulation | selection state only | P | code filters to APT_PACKAGE; no test |
| B11 | `/usr/bin/apt-mark` in the target sudo grant | named in the hint | U | apt:`test_apt_mark_is_in_the_target_sudo_command_list` |

## C. apt repository config — sources, keys, pins, apt.conf (D-11, D-12, D-13, D-27)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Source file missing on target, key present on source | INSTALL | U | apt:`test_source_with_key_present_on_source_yields_plain_install` |
| C2 | Source file whose `Signed-By:`/`signed-by=` names a key absent on the source | REPORT_ONLY + dangling detail, never installable | U | apt:`test_source_with_dangling_keyring_reference_is_flagged_not_installable` |
| C3 | Same, but the source file is *changed* rather than missing | also downgraded to REPORT_ONLY | U | apt:`test_changed_source_with_dangling_keyring_reference_is_downgraded_to_report_only` |
| C4 | deb822 `.sources` vs legacy `.list` | format recorded per file, never normalised; identity is the filename | U | apt:`test_deb822_and_legacy_source_each_record_own_format` |
| C5 | Same repo described by both a `.list` and a `.sources` file | two distinct items, both visible | P | identity-by-filename tested; the coexistence case itself is not |
| C6 | Key present per-repo vs global-trust with the same filename | distinct item ids | U | apt:`test_per_repo_and_global_trust_keys_are_distinct_item_ids` |
| C7 | Key digests identical on both machines | no diff, no content fetch | U | apt:`test_key_matching_digest_on_both_sides_produces_no_diff` |

## Coverage is genuinely broad
Per-manager diff taxonomies, the apt repo-group transaction (backup → write → update → rollback), D-30 collateral in all six variants, the snippet lifecycle including the non-additive push guard, review grouping/defaults/abort, dry-run, per-item failure isolation, exit-code derivation, folder_sync exclusions, the snapd hold window, and the new step gate are all covered — mostly at unit level, with 7 VM tests for whole-run contracts.

1. **skip-always never silences an apt or snap hold.** The decision file entry is written — there's a test for the write — and then ignored forever: `collect_hold_sets()`'s output and `_diff_snap_holds`'s inputs never pass `filter_inert`, and `filter_inert` matches `snap:<name>`, not `snap:hold:<name>`. The hold/unhold item reappears in every later review. Flatpak masks *are* correct, so the three managers #208 D3 calls uniform are not.
2. **skip-always on any REPORT_ONLY item records nothing.** Version mismatches, repo-unavailable packages and pin echoes get the three-way choice and "skip always" silently no-ops (`_record_permanent_skips` filters to INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE). Snapd rejects `snap install --revision=N` for a classic snap, so each becomes a per-item failure. Sideloaded snaps (`x1` revisions) are the same shape. This one is code-verified but the snapd behaviour itself I did not exercise here.

## Two of your example narratives are not implemented
- No "P was the only package from that source — remove the source and key too?" prompt. Source/key removals propagate only because those files vanished on the source machine, as independent unticked items.
- Nothing links a repo/key removal to a machine-specific package on the target that still needs it. In example 3, source S *is* offered for removal on B with no awareness of R; keeping it requires a second skip-always on the source item.

Your example 1 works, but by omission: the manifest is `apt-mark showmanual` only, so dependency-only Q is invisible to every branch — and **no test states that**, which is the load-bearing assumption of the whole apt model (A10/N8).

## Biggest gaps in behaviour that is otherwise correct
- No test asserts a hold/mask renders as "Hold …"/"Unmask …" instead of under an install/remove group — the one behavioural promise of #208 D3.
- No idempotency test anywhere: converge once, second run shows an empty review.
- Missing: apt install-before-hold ordering, hold on an absent package, remote removed while a ref still uses it, source+key removed together, and the VM check #208 D9 explicitly promised for the per-snap-hold capture-timing assumption.

- the bugs you found to be challenged and fixed if needed

A skip-always decision recorded against a block-state item is written to the machine-local decision file and then never honoured: the same item is re-emitted as a diff on every later run.

Repo: /home/janfr/dev/pc-switcher, branch gsd/phase-02-package-management-sync.

Close a confirmed code-vs-docs gap: the batched checkbox review offers only TWO outcomes (apply / skip once) for every regular item, while ADR-020 D-07 and `docs/jobs/package-sync.md` promise a three-way choice including "skip always".

## Ownership — several agents are working concurrently

You own: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/review.py`, `docs/jobs/package-sync.md`, `docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md`, `.planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md`, `.planning/STATE.md`, and a NEW test file `tests/unit/jobs/test_review_skip_always.py`.

You MUST NOT edit: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py`, `apt_sync.py`, `snap_sync.py`, `flatpak_sync.py`, `items.py`, `state.py` (another agent is fixing a defect in those), nor any EXISTING test file under tests/ (other agents own them). If you believe a change outside your files is required, STOP and report it instead of making it.

## Scope (decided by the user — implement exactly this)

Offer skip-always for **actionable items only**: diffs whose action is INSTALL, CHANGE or REMOVE — which includes the block-state items (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`, `flatpak:mask:`), for which `docs/jobs/package-sync.md:107` promises it explicitly. REPORT_ONLY items (version mismatch, repo-unavailable, held/pinned echo) stay informational and are NOT offered skip-always: a version drift has no honest "holder" machine, and recording one would silently stop that package syncing altogether — much stronger than "stop reporting this".

## Requirements for the implementation

Read `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/review.py` fully first, plus `_record_permanent_skips` in sync_core.py (read only — do not edit) to see what the write path already accepts. `Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS` and its persistence already exist and work for actionable items; only the UI path to produce it is missing.

- Add the third choice to the ordinary checkbox flow. A reasonable shape: after a group's checkbox returns, run a second prompt over the UNTICKED entries of that group asking which should be permanent ("never offer this again on this machine"). Choose the interaction you judge best within the existing questionary + Rich Live constraints — but it must not turn the review back into a per-item question queue (D-24: the user wants to tick items off a list). If every entry was ticked, prompt nothing.
- Must compose with everything the module already guarantees: `ui.pause()`/`resume()` in a `finally`, the blocking `.ask()` dispatched via `asyncio.to_thread` (ADR-005), untrusted labels wrapped in `Text` (never bare `str` into a Panel/console — the MarkupError guard).
- Ctrl-C / EOF at the new prompt aborts the WHOLE sync (`SyncAbortedByUser`), consistent with the existing checkbox and unreproducible rules. Never a silent per-item fallthrough.
- Non-interactive runs (`is_interactive` False) prompt for nothing and still return everything SKIP_ONCE (D-26) — unchanged.
- The `PCSWITCHER_PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION` hatch is unchanged.
- The `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` and `COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION` groups keep their own existing flows — the new prompt must not apply to them.
- REPORT_ONLY groups must not offer it (see scope above).

## Docs

- `docs/jobs/package-sync.md`: the three-way choice is now real for actionable items; state plainly that informational items (version mismatch, no repo candidate, pin echo) are reported only and are resolved by fixing the underlying condition, not by a machine-specific mark.
- `docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md`: add a brief amending note recording that D-07's three-way decision applies to actionable item classes, with the reason REPORT_ONLY is excluded (no holder machine; VERSION_MISMATCH in particular). Follow the file's existing amendment style (see its 2026-07-24 notes). Terse, no history or narration of this session.
- `.planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md` (~line 206) and `.planning/STATE.md` (~lines 133, 146) record this as known work and reference STALE paths (`jobs/package_review.py`, `jobs/package_sync_core.py` — now `jobs/packages/review.py`, `jobs/packages/sync_core.py`). Update those entries to reflect that it is now implemented, and fix the paths.

Repo writing style is terse: no "previously", no dated incidents, no restating the change. Markdown rules: no `---` separators, no bold-as-heading, no mid-sentence hard wrapping.

## Tests (new file only)

Cover: the third choice produces SKIP_ALWAYS for an unticked actionable item; a ticked item is unaffected; REPORT_ONLY groups are never offered it; unreproducible/collateral groups keep their own flow; non-interactive prompts nothing; Ctrl-C/EOF at the new prompt aborts the whole sync; the live display is paused and resumed even when the new prompt raises; hold and mask items (INSTALL and REMOVE directions) can be made permanent. Match the style of the existing tests/unit/jobs/test_package_review.py (read it for helpers and idiom, but do not edit it).

`uv run ruff format . && uv run ruff check . && uv run basedpyright && uv run pytest tests/unit -q` — all clean. Concurrent agents are committing; if their in-flight work breaks your run, re-run and do not "fix" their files.
